# Free reading: UI boards and implementation handoff

2026-11-03 behavior revision: follow the owner's
[simple live plan](../../research/free-content/SIMPLE_LIVE_PLAN.md). Reuse these
approved visual styles with one live source per paper search, source switching,
and outbound website searches for deferred connectors. The earlier multi-source
cache/budget/session behavior is historical, rather than a storage prerequisite.

Status: **approved UI reference; implementation in progress.** Dated 2026-11-01.
Current decisions, implemented slices and remaining gates are in
[the implementation record](../../research/free-content/IMPLEMENTATION.md).
The [implementation screen review](../../research/free-content/UI_REVIEW.md)
compares all fourteen boards on phone/desktop in all three reading lights and
records the fixes, evidence and deliberate data-dependent differences.

Implement free-book and research-paper discovery from this document, the boards
in [`boards/`](boards/) (gallery: [index.html](index.html)) and the research in
[`../../research/free-content/`](../../research/free-content/README.md). The
research README's "UI proposal and owner decisions" section records the owner's
answers; they are repeated in [Decisions](#1-decisions) below. Where this file
and the architecture proposal disagree on UI, this file wins; on backend
contracts, [architecture.md](../../research/free-content/architecture.md) wins.

The same boards are on a private Design canvas for owner review:
https://claude.ai/artifact/NHwYSSaU4VGXDt2Pp9aA4X. The repo copies are the
reference for implementation.

## Viewing the boards

From the repository root run `python3 -m http.server 4196` and open
http://localhost:4196/docs/design/2026-11-free-content/index.html. Add
`?light=lamplight` or `?light=ink` to any board. Phone boards are 390×844;
`DeskFreeSearch` is fluid and drawn at 1280 wide. Inside a board, links between
boards work and links to hosts do nothing.

**All records are samples.** Project Gutenberg IDs, titles and the Gutenberg
rights wording are real. Every paper, author, journal, DOI (the `10.5555` test
prefix), arXiv ID and children's story is invented. Never copy board records
into fixtures as if they were real catalog data.

Boards follow the existing app: reading-light tokens from
[`../2026-10-mobile/reading-lights.css`](../2026-10-mobile/reading-lights.css),
Newsreader headings, system sans body, 44px touch targets and the four-tab bar.
Covers are drawn as coloured blocks because no cover art is redistributed; in
the app use real covers when a source supplies them and the existing
placeholder otherwise.

## 1. Decisions

1. **Keep the four tabs.** Free to read and Papers are scopes inside Search.
2. **Free books and papers can be saved to the shelf.** See
   [§6](#6-saving-to-the-shelf): the storage shape still needs an engineering
   decision before coding.
3. **Unclear access is hidden by default, and marked when shown.** The Free to
   read list never mixes unclear items in silently.
4. **No "include previews and loans" option** in the first release.
5. **Daily limit:** say the wide paper search is at today's limit. Do not name
   the provider to readers.
6. **Children's pilot:** English, Hindi and Tamil, using each publisher's own
   reading levels.
7. **Library link-back:** a free book offers "Prefer print? Find it at
   [library]". It runs a title/author search; it never asserts the two are the
   same edition.
8. **Rights text stays generic:** the source's own statement plus a prompt to
   check your country's rules. No per-country legal claims.
9. **Request identification** uses the existing public contact. Use is
   non-commercial. Traffic expectations and quotas are set later, so build
   budgets as configuration, not constants.

## Owner clarification: free source accounts (2026-11-01)

The owner clarified: free source login is acceptable, and those books must be
searchable with a link to the book. Verified `free_account_required` books now
appear under **Free account required**, with the condition repeated on the card
and before the source reading link. Anonymous reading remains distinct. Unknown
registration charges, previews, loans and paid access remain excluded. These are
accounts on the reading site, not a MyBookshelf account feature. The updated
implementation and source evidence supersede the old registration exclusion in
the boards; the remaining approved layout and shelf behavior still apply.

## 2. Scope

First release (matches research Phase A/B):

- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

Not in the first release: previews/loans, Standard Ebooks, DIKSHA/NCERT, CORE,
HAL, Zenodo, bioRxiv/medRxiv as live sources (show "Not connected yet" if
listed), embedded readers, downloads proxied through our server, accounts.

## 3. Navigation and routes

Search keeps one route, `/app/search`. The scope control becomes three
segments:

| Segment | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Library books | Today's search. **Keep the existing "All books / [library]" control** as a second row under this segment only; the boards omit it for space. ISBN scanning stays here. |
| Free to read | Free books and stories (`kinds` = book, learning_resource; children's pilot via its tile). |
| Papers | Articles, preprints, chapters (`kinds` = article, preprint, chapter, thesis, report). Query field also accepts DOI and arXiv IDs. |

Proposed URL state so back/forward and sharing work: `/app/search?scope=free&q=…`
and `/app/search?scope=papers&q=…`; no `scope` means Library books, which keeps
existing links valid. Content detail: `/app/read/:contentKey`, using the opaque
`Item.key` from the content API. Do not reuse `/app/books/:bookKey`: content
keys are a separate identity space (architecture §2, §3). The children's pilot
is `/app/search?scope=free&collection=children`. All `/app/` routes stay noindex
and out of the sitemap.

Tab bar: Search stays active for every board except the library book page,
where Shelf is active as today.

## 4. Boards

Each row names the board, what it proves, and the data it needs from
`POST /api/v2/content/search` / `resolve`.

| Board | What it shows | Data and behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FreeStart` | Free to read with no query: four browse tiles (Classic literature, Open textbooks, Children's stories, Research papers) and recent free searches. | Tiles are static links into scopes/collections. Recent searches reuse the existing search memory, tagged with scope. Tile subtitles name the source. |
| `FreeBookResults` | Results for a free-book query, filter chips, loaded count with a Sources link, and the hidden-unclear notice. | Show **loaded counts**, never a global total ("3 free books shown · from Project Gutenberg"). Anonymous `free_full_text` items and a separately labelled `free_account_required` group are listed. Items with `unknown`/`metadata_only` access for this query are counted in the notice; "Show them, labelled" appends them under an "Unclear access" heading (see `DeskFreeSearch`). `preview`, `borrow`, unknown-price `registration` and `restricted` are never shown. Verified free accounts follow the owner clarification above. Filter chips: language, format, kind. Unsupported filters must be disabled with a reason, not silently ignored. |
| `FreeBookDetail` | One free edition: Read at host (primary), format links, rights, other free versions, library link-back, Save. | Primary action is the location's `readerUrl` or `landingUrl`, labelled "Read at [host]". Format buttons only for supplied `downloads` (label by MIME: EPUB, Kindle, Plain text, PDF). Rights box: source statement verbatim plus generic country note; footer "From [source] · checked [relative time]" from `evidence.observedAt`. "Other free versions" lists related items only when `relations` carry source evidence; each row states how it differs ("Separate recording", "Different source text"). |
| `LibraryBookFreeEdition` | Existing `/app/books/:bookKey` page with a new "Also free to read" card under availability. | Show only when a free item is linked by an exact identifier or the Open Library work ID (`workId`) with source evidence. Never by title similarity. Copy must say it is a different edition. Link opens `/app/read/:contentKey`. If resolution fails or is slow, omit the section; do not show an error on the library page. |
| `PaperResults` | Paper results with type pill, title, authors, container/year, and access line naming index and host. | Pill from `kind` (+ `version` for preprints: "Preprint · v3"). Source-supplied flags ("Correction listed", "Retracted") as a second pill in `--chk`/`--err`, worded as the source's claim. Access line: "Free · Found via [index], read at [host]" when they differ; "Free · HTML, PDF at arXiv" when the index is the host. Authors truncate to three plus "+ N". |
| `PaperDetail` | Preprint with versions, published version relation, licence, Save. | Versions are separate rows linking to each version. The published version is a relation with its own access state; never substitute it for the preprint or show the preprint's licence on it. Licence line uses `license.id` when present; when absent, say "Licence not stated". |
| `SourcesSheet` | Bottom sheet listing each source and its status for this query. | One row per entry in the response `sources` array. Status copy: ok → "N shown" (and "M already listed" for duplicates); not chosen by planner → "Not searched this time" + "Search it" action; disabled flag → "Not connected yet"; timeout/throttled/quota → see states below. Reuse `ui/Sheet.tsx`. |
| `Loading` | Per-source progress while searching. | Rows update as sources answer (ok / searching / queued). Results stream in below. Static skeleton blocks; no shimmer. Copy states the 5-second cap. |
| `PartialCoverage` | One source timed out; others' results shown. | Notice above results with "Try [source] again", which retries only that source using the search session cursor. Count line says "N of M sources answered". |
| `SourcesDown` | Every source failed with no cached results. | `role="alert"`. Must say this does not mean there's no free copy. Actions: Try again; Search library books instead (switches scope, keeps query). Never render as zero results. |
| `NoFreeCopy` | All sources answered; none has a free copy. | Lists each searched source with "0 matches". Primary action: check the selected library (or "Choose a library" when none). No previews/loans option. |
| `BudgetUsed` | Broad paper index at its daily limit; specialist results shown. | Notice: "Wide paper search is at today's limit. It resets tomorrow…" Do not name the provider. Show results from the remaining sources. |
| `ChildrensPilot` | Reviewed children's set: language chips (English, हिन्दी, தமிழ்), publisher levels 1–4, story cards with credits and licence. | Copy must say it is a reviewed starter set, not every free children's book. Level is "as the publisher labels it"; don't map levels across publishers or infer age. Credits show author, illustrator and translator roles from `contributors`. Translations are separate items; the card may say "also in [languages]". Set `lang` on non-English labels. |
| `DeskFreeSearch` | Desktop: navigation rail, results list and detail side by side; shows the expanded "Unclear access" group. | Selecting a result updates the right pane and the URL; Back returns to the previous selection. Unclear items carry the hollow `--chk` marker and "Access unclear · may be a loan, check at the source", plus a Hide link. Follow existing desktop layout rules in [`../2026-10-mobile/DESKTOP_PLAN.md`](../2026-10-mobile/DESKTOP_PLAN.md). |

## 5. Components and existing code

| Need | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three-segment scope | `ui/scan/ScanPage.tsx` | Extend the existing `.search-scope.segment-control`. Keep the library sub-toggle and ISBN scanning under Library books only. |
| Content result row | new `ui/content/ContentResult.tsx` | Two variants: book (cover 52×78) and paper (no cover, pill row). Don't overload `ui/scan/SearchResult.tsx`. |
| Access line | new `ui/content/AccessLine.tsx` | Filled dot `--ok` for free; hollow dot `--chk` for unclear. Text always states the state; colour is never the only signal. |
| Kind/flag pill | new `ui/content/KindPill.tsx` | Preprint `--ref`, article/chapter `--ink2`, correction `--chk`, retraction `--err`. |
| Coverage/status notices | `ui/Notice.tsx` | Partial, limit and down states. |
| Sources sheet | `ui/Sheet.tsx` | Focus trap and Escape exactly as existing sheets. |
| Detail page | new `ui/content/ContentPage.tsx` at `/app/read/:contentKey` | Outbound links: `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`, visible ↗ and an accessible name ending "(opens [host])". |
| "Also free to read" | `ui/book/BookPage.tsx` | Separate fetch after the main book loads; must not delay or fail the availability block. |
| Copy | `uiMessages.ts` | Add strings from the boards verbatim (they were written for this app's voice). |
| API client | `api.ts` | `contentSearch`, `contentResolve`; abort on scope/query change. |

Server work is in architecture.md §2 and §5 (`server/services/content/`,
`server/public-v2/content.js`). The UI relies on these response fields:
`items[].{key, kind, title, contributors, version, container, publishedAt,
languages, locations[].{access, landingUrl, readerUrl, downloads, license,
evidence}, relations, provenance}`, `coverage`, `sources[].{id, status,
returned, retryable}`, `nextCursor`. Map `sources[].status` values as follows:
`ok`, `empty`, `timeout`, `throttled`, `quota_exhausted`, `unsupported`,
`disabled`, `not_selected`. The last one is needed for "Not searched this time";
add it to the contract if the server work hasn't.

## 6. Saving to the shelf

The owner wants free books and papers saveable. Today `savedBooks` holds
`RecentBook` records keyed by `bookKey` with ISBN/work identity
(`client/src/v2/localState.ts`, storage key `mybookshelf.anonymous-web.v1`,
version 1, cap 100). Content items have no ISBN and a different key space.

Before coding, the implementing agent should write a short decision covering:
a distinct saved-item kind (for example `{ kind: 'content', contentKey, title,
authors, itemKind, host }`) instead of faking a `bookKey`; a storage version
bump with migration that keeps every existing saved book; how the shelf draws
items without covers (paper spines); whether content counts toward the
100-item cap; and alignment with the planned account sync (STATUS.md, account
work), which must not gain a competing identity system. The Save button in the
boards uses the existing bookmark control and `aria-pressed` pattern.

## 7. Copy and accessibility rules

- Keep "free to read" separate from reuse rights in all copy. "Free" means free
  to read at the source, never "free to download and share".
- Failures are never absence: timeout, limit, down and unsupported states each
  have their own copy; none says "no results".
- Name the host in every outbound action ("Read at Project Gutenberg").
- Status is conveyed by text plus shape (filled vs hollow dot, pill label), not
  colour alone. Check contrast in Daylight, Lamplight and Ink.
- Live regions: loading progress `role="status"` (polite); `SourcesDown`
  `role="alert"`.
- Respect reduced motion; boards use no animation and the app shouldn't add any
  for these states.
- Language chips and story titles in Hindi/Tamil carry `lang`.

## 8. Acceptance checklist

Run the release checks in AGENTS.md plus:

- Each board's state reachable from fixtures (sanitised, no live network in unit
  tests), on mobile and desktop, in all three reading lights.
- Preview, borrow and metadata-only fixtures never appear in Free to read;
  unknown appears only after "Show them" and is marked.
- One source failing keeps other results; all failing shows `SourcesDown`, not
  an empty list; quota shows `BudgetUsed` copy without the provider name.
- Paging adds results without duplicates or skips; counts say "shown".
- Preprint and published version stay separate; translations stay separate.
- The library book page with a free edition renders the card only with
  identifier/work evidence; a title-only near match renders nothing.
- Saving and unsaving a free book and a paper survives reload, and existing
  saved books survive the storage migration.
- Existing ISBN, library and shelf journeys are unchanged.

## 9. Still open (engineering, not owner)

- Shelf storage shape for content items (§6).
- `not_selected` source status in the response contract.
- Quota numbers: set later per decision 9; ship with configurable budgets and
  the `BudgetUsed` state wired.
- Children's pilot record list and feed/curation process (research Phase C).

# Additional source research and Book Dash delivery

The owner asked Codex to research many other sources on 2026-11-01. This is
Codex-owned work; a publisher feed or a reviewed candidate list is not an input
requested from the owner. [FCD08 #140](https://github.com/ddk220-light/MyBookshelf-web/issues/140)
tracks the next delivered connector and source survey. The [probe ledger](evidence/2026-11-01/additional-sources.json)
records current observations and their limits.

## Connected next: Book Dash

The public WordPress book type exposes source-native edition IDs and an explicit
language taxonomy. The catalog reported 1,116 language-edition entries and its
English taxonomy reported 214 when checked. A bounded **30-English-edition**
subset is now bundled and searchable alongside Gutenberg, textbooks and the
reviewed StoryWeaver set. This does not claim complete source coverage.

The [official catalog](https://bookdash.org/books/) and
[reuse policy](https://bookdash.org/re-using-the-book-dash-content/) state that
Book Dash books are free and published under CC BY 4.0. Original creator roles
are preserved: writer, illustrator, designer, editor and any supplied translator
or photographer. The source supplies no publisher reading level for this
subset; none is inferred. These books participate in ordinary Free to read
searches; the separate EN/HI/TA pilot remains explicitly a reviewed starter set.

The sampled [Let’s Go Looking](https://bookdash.org/books/lets-go-looking/)
reader displayed all 14 supplied book-page images without a source account.
The app flow on phone/desktop verified search → source link → save → reload →
reopen, original credits, and 320px/200% text reflow without page errors. The
app stores metadata and source links; no book text, images or files are stored.
No PDF/EPUB button is invented from a source-files folder or image gallery.

The importer bounds source responses and record counts, spaces requests,
honors bounded source cooldowns, rejects redirects/off-host readers and missing
public galleries/credits, and publishes atomically with shrink protection.
After initial selection, refresh pins the same native IDs. New titles cannot
push an existing saved edition out of the bounded subset. A live second import
retained all 30 identities. Missing pinned metadata stops refresh for review.

```sh
python tools/content/import_bookdash.py --max-records 30 --output server/data/content/bookdash.json
python -m unittest discover -s tools/content -v
node tools/content/audit_snapshots.mjs
```

The daily reviewed catalog workflow includes Book Dash. Positive access evidence
expires after 24 hours; failed refresh never renews stale claims. Catalog search
requires no Redis. The first scheduled run follows default-branch merge and
remains a release check.

## Other sources checked

| Source | Fresh result | Remaining work before connection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Wikisource](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Main_page) | Public metadata APIs returned stable page IDs in English, Hindi and Tamil. | Resolve redirects, distinguish work/edition lists and transclusions from complete editions, preserve contributors and per-text rights. The sampled Hindi title redirected. Do not treat namespace 0 or HTTP 200 alone as a readable book. |
| [DOAB](https://www.doabooks.org/en/librarians/doab-metadata) | Official OAI-PMH Identify returned the DOAB repository. The librarians page links the current metadata documentation. | Import the documented richer metadata, inspect book/chapter type, licences and supplied reading locations; use exact DOI/handle/ISBN evidence when reconciling OAPEN overlap. The earlier guessed documentation URLs returned 404. |
| [OAPEN](https://library.oapen.org/) | OAI Identify/formats and a 100-record Dublin Core sample worked; sample rights fields include explicit open-access semantics. | Verify current metadata terms, map versions/chapters and individual licences, sample actual supplied full-book links and implement incremental refresh. No download location was inferred from an index-wide label. |
| [African Storybook](https://www.africanstorybook.org/) | Public site loaded. | Review individual story/language/level/credit/licence/reader evidence and a supported export or discovery protocol. Homepage access is not connector readiness. |
| [Storybooks Canada](https://storybookscanada.ca/) | Actual English/Hindi readers loaded with original contributor roles and per-item CC BY 3.0 in the sampled book. | Verify a feed/curation contract and relevant language coverage. The sampled Tamil reader was 404; this does not prove the whole Tamil collection absent. Preserve its licence rather than substituting CC BY 4.0. |
| [Internet Archive](https://archive.org/developers/) | Public advanced search returned text-item metadata. | Inspect per-item files, rights and access. A text item, the opensource collection, a free account and a borrowing entitlement are different facts. Previews/loans remain excluded. |
| [ICDL](https://www.childrenslibrary.org/) | Public homepage loaded. | Verify currently usable individual readers, current permissions/attribution, languages and stable identities; no comprehensive feed has been established. |

# Executing the free-knowledge expansion

Proposed operating plan, 2026-11-05. Implements the direction in the
[expansion plan](EXPANSION_PLAN.md) and its six category playbooks. This document
sets a workflow; it does not start scheduled jobs or claim newly enabled sources.

The owner subsequently authorized continued research and selected a
[Git-tracked JSON registry](registry/README.md) instead of a SQL database.
Its [goal and continuation cursor](registry/goal.json) record that work.
Ten stored retrieval examples are an additional research checkpoint, not a
replacement for the full qualification gates below.

## Recommendation: batch the research, limit active engineering, release often

Use a rolling pipeline with two overlapping workstreams: **source research** and
**product delivery**. Research several candidates together; select a small group
that shares a supported retrieval pattern; implement one connector family at a
time, with independently verified mappings for each origin. Ship a ready source
without waiting for every candidate in its research batch.

| Approach | Useful part | Limitation | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fixed number of sources every day | Creates a regular research habit | An easy catalog and a complex land-record service take very different effort; pressure to hit a count can reward superficial checks | Use research-session ranges and time budgets, never a daily activation quota |
| Finish one source completely before considering another | Keeps ownership and acceptance clear | A missing feed, restrictive terms or unavailable key can stop all progress; repeated one-off integrations miss shared patterns | Keep one active engineering family, with alternative qualified origins available |
| Research all categories before implementing anything | Gives broad coverage visibility | Delays learning from real users, operating costs and deployed source behavior | Survey incrementally and begin delivery when the first useful source passes its gates |
| Rolling small batches | Combines comparison, reusable engineering and frequent usable output | Requires a shared register and explicit limits on unfinished work | Recommended workflow |

The 300 candidate memberships and 60 distinct deep reviews in the master plan
are **cumulative first-program limits**, not an upfront research assignment.
Discovery, qualification, implementation and maintenance overlap. Reaching 100
means retaining useful, searchable coverage, not accumulating unchecked URLs.

## 1. Work queue and state transitions

Use the existing Git repository for the research register, evidence and source
manifest. Use the existing GitHub project for selected implementation stories.
Do not create one GitHub issue for every raw lead or provision a hosted database.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Candidate] --> B[Triage]
    B --> C[Probe]
    C --> D[Qualified]
    D --> E[Ready for implementation]
    E --> F[Implement]
    F --> G[Verify]
    G --> H[Enabled]
    B --> X[Deferred or rejected]
    C --> X
    F --> X
    H --> Y[Suspended]
    Y --> C
```

Transitions are evidence-based. If a permission or API assumption fails during
implementation, revise its research record; do not keep calling it qualified
under the disproved route. A deferred source can re-enter when its stated trigger
changes. Suspended sources lose their healthy-enabled designation until repaired.

| State | Required result before moving forward |
| --- | --- |
| Candidate | Canonical operator/domain, discovery link, intended content/industry/public-record coverage; duplicate check |
| Triaged | Plausible free content, supported retrieval route to inspect, documented terms/cost leads, relevance to an identified coverage gap |
| Probed | Reproducible requests/import sample, real native records and actual destinations, query capability and access observations |
| Qualified | All mandatory gates in the master plan pass for the declared subset; evidence date, scope, limits and maintainer recorded |
| Ready | Selected for the next small delivery batch, dependencies and credentials resolved, benchmark and source contract agreed; new UI requirements reviewed where needed |
| Implementing | One bounded story with source mapping, retrieval, access handling, fixtures and refresh behavior |
| Verifying | Adapter/API checks, real source observations and appropriate hosted/browser journeys pass; rollback and operations record prepared |
| Enabled | Released source is reachable in its declared product flow; exact release and live proof recorded |
| Deferred/rejected/suspended | Concrete reason, affected capability, next action or reconsideration trigger; no misleading positive access claim |

Retain origin IDs independently from connector IDs, category memberships and
industry tags. For example, an aggregator connector can expose several publishers,
but each claimed origin still needs evidence of actual coverage and access.

## 2. Capacity and limits on work in progress

Start with these defaults for one lead implementer; calibrate after two cycles:

| Queue | Initial limit | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Newly selected triage batch | 15–20 unique origins | Enough alternatives to compare without opening a huge active backlog |
| Deep probes in progress | Four origins at once | Keeps incomplete permission/access questions manageable |
| Qualified and selected for delivery | Three to five origins | Leaves alternatives if one stalls; revalidate evidence before use |
| Active engineering | One connector family and at most two origin mappings concurrently | Limits overlapping edits and unfinished integrations |
| Final verification/release | One small batch | Makes failures attributable and rollback clear |

Raw leads can stay in the register without becoming active work. If the ready
queue is full, focus on delivery or a specific underrepresented category rather
than continuing to fill it. If it is empty, shift a session into qualification.

On a **research-focused session**, a starting range is 8–12 quick triages or
1–3 deep probes, depending on complexity. These are alternatives within the
available work budget, not additive daily requirements. Coding and release
sessions have no source-discovery quota. Track usable output and elapsed effort.

Use short decision timeboxes:

- **Triage:** around 10–15 minutes per origin to identify a plausible route and
  obvious exclusions. Missing evidence means unproven, not approved.
- **Initial deep probe:** around 30–90 minutes. A promising unresolved case can
  receive one explicitly scoped 2–4-hour technical spike with a question and exit
  criterion. Time spent does not relax qualification requirements.
- **External dependency:** move to deferred with a trigger such as published API
  documentation, an available free key, clarified permission or a scheduled
  review date. Do not retry it every day or hold the release for it.

Routine implementation decisions stay with the implementer. Owner input is only
needed for a real product decision or external action requiring it, such as new
costs, source outreach or a newly designed interaction—not for every source.

## 3. A practical five-session delivery cycle

A cycle is approximately a working week when capacity permits. It is not a
promise of unattended work every calendar day. New connector families may span
multiple cycles; existing mappings may move faster.

| Session | Primary work | Reviewable output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — Select and screen | Check existing-source health, choose a theme, screen 15–20 queued candidates; split this across sessions if time requires | Shortlist of four to six, duplicate decisions, clear rejected/deferred reasons |
| 2 — Prove the useful routes | Deep-review a small subset; obtain real results, validate access/terms and benchmark relevance | Qualified records with measured scope; choose one retrieval family and initial origins |
| 3–4 — Build and verify continuously | Expand concrete tasks for selected stories, implement the first mapping, then another supported by the same pattern; write meaningful failure/access tests | Small PRs, reproducible source probes, working preview; no untested bulk enabling |
| 5 — Release and learn | Complete end-to-end verification, release the ready subset, check production and operating evidence | Verified live coverage, release record, measured effort and next batch recommendation |

Keep a modest research queue running while delivery proceeds. Delegated
researchers can inspect independent categories from the playbooks and return
evidence-backed recommendations. The lead reconciles identities, permissions,
shared quotas and priority. Parallel work is useful for discovery and independent
tests; additional agents do not multiply provider rate limits. Give code workers
non-overlapping files/worktrees and keep shared connector changes coordinated.

Plan releases in **small batches of up to three to five ready origins**. One
well-tested source can be released on its own; an unfinished neighbor stays off.
There is no minimum weekly activation count. Repeat checks only when changes,
expired observations or failures justify them; documentation-only edits need
documentation checks rather than the complete application suite.

## 4. Choose the next batch by useful coverage and shared implementation

Apply the master plan's mandatory gates first, then its priority weights. Compare
incremental content/language/local coverage, query/access quality, maintenance
burden and implementation effort. A large catalog consisting mostly of already
available records can be less useful than a small regional-language collection.

Select a delivery theme, not an arbitrary bundle of unrelated websites:

- **Book/catalog theme:** an official reusable book export and additional origins
  demonstrably covered by it. Reuse the current book search/detail/shelf flow.
- **Industry guidance theme:** agricultural extension or construction/manufacturing
  training catalogs that share document/learning-resource mappings and useful
  task metadata. Implement cross-cutting tags with evidence for each assignment.
- **Public-document theme:** government reports, acts or civic records with a
  supported document API/export and explicit jurisdiction/version handling.
- **Geospatial theme:** one supported catalog/native query pattern, first a US
  case and an India case when both qualify; distinguish map discovery from
  feature/parcel lookup rather than pretending all services offer both.

An index with broad coverage can be valuable early. Verify source attribution
for each underlying origin before counting it. Generalizing a connector is
justified by a second qualified use case; avoid building a universal connector
framework before seeing those cases.

Keep breadth visible during selection. Over the first two cycles, aim to assess
at least one candidate from each of the six playbooks, with both US and India
public-information candidates. Record every category/industry not yet sampled.
Reserve about one fifth of ongoing research capacity for neglected categories or
languages so easy English-language paper APIs do not consume the whole program.
This is a research allocation; unsuitable sources do not get a lower admission bar.

## 5. Suggested opening sequence

These are conditional delivery waves. The source examples are candidates from the
research playbooks, not promises that their APIs or permissions already pass.

| Wave | Work to reach and expand into tasks | Exit / effect on next wave |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 — Establish the working baseline | Recheck currently enabled source behavior and freshness; inspect existing reviewed-refresh failure, including StoryWeaver; define source register and a small repeatable benchmark | Existing problems have concrete repair/defer decisions. Fix any shared blocker relevant to a selected release; an isolated source failure does not stop unrelated work |
| 1 — First useful book expansion | Compare two or three likely reusable catalogs, such as the documented DOAB/OAPEN route and an India-focused book/textbook candidate; select the first qualified route | Ship a working, bounded book-search expansion with fresh evidence and a repeatable refresh path. A single source is a valid first release |
| 2 — Repeatability and industry relevance | Prove reuse with another qualified origin; add agriculture/construction/manufacturing/logistics guidance where current content kinds fit | Shared mapping proves useful; task/industry metadata and source tests work without losing native identities. Review any new browse/filter design before implementing it |
| 3 — Public documents and maps | Qualify US/India law/civic/property/geology candidates in parallel with earlier waves; design and deliver the first supported record/map capability | A reader can perform the declared query and open the official result; unsupported jurisdiction/mode is explicit. Record discovery and feature lookup have separate acceptance tests |
| 4 — Wider formats and sustained expansion | Add audio, reference entries, archival objects and other cohorts as their retrieval and presentation contracts become ready | Maintain a stream of tested releases while advancing each category/industry toward its next qualification milestone |

Research for Wave 3 starts during Wave 1; US/India public records and maps should
not disappear behind the easier book work. Preserve the twelve-origin US/India
public-information allocation inside the overall 60-review pilot. The full
300-membership survey and 60-review allowance can be spread across several cycles.

The initial ten deep-review slots should mix approximately three book/children's
origins, two India-focused industry/learning origins, two public-information
origins (one US, one India), and one each in audio, scholarly research, and
reference/culture/media. Apply overlap and availability honestly; use the result
to revise effort estimates, not to infer that all categories have been qualified.

Refresh is part of each source's delivery. Establish independent import validation
and failure reporting where needed so one source's review failure does not erase
valid results elsewhere. Never advance observation timestamps to make an expired
source appear fresh. If the existing refresh policy is too costly for a proposed
catalog, resolve that operational question before enabling it.

## 6. Stories to expand when they are reached

Use a batch-level issue linking the selected source records. Create the specific
stories below only for the next active batch. A shared connector can have one
engineering story, with separate origin evidence/mapping acceptance; avoid
hundreds of empty source issues or a single enormous release PR.

| Story | Concrete tasks | Done when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source qualification | Identify operator/duplicates, inspect current terms/free limits, run known-item and topical or structured-query probes, check actual destinations, complete review record | Declared subset and query modes pass the master gates; exclusions and expiry documented |
| Retrieval and mapping | Define allowed endpoint/import route, native identities, paging, cancellation, limits, language/access mapping and origin attribution; implement representative fixtures | Real sample works; malformed/partial/restricted/timeout/limit cases are handled correctly; no paid fallback |
| Search integration | Expose the selected source and supported intent; route queries, preserve pagination and detail resolution, show coverage and unavailable states | Search and exact item resolution work without hidden source switching or misleading global-coverage claims |
| New content/interaction design, when needed | Write concise product, UI and engineering notes; produce an artifact for new industry browsing, record input or map/media result representation; obtain the owner's review of that concrete artifact | Approved behavior and fields are clear. Existing approved book flows can continue without waiting for unrelated new UI |
| End-to-end release | Test API and browser search → detail → official destination → save/reload where applicable; inspect phone/desktop and reading lights; deploy checked code and verify canonical production under existing authorization | Actual release/source evidence and rollback are recorded; the working scope is enabled |
| Operations | Define refresh/deletion behavior, source owner, review cadence, free-capacity checks and suspension conditions; prove the applicable refresh path | The source can stay truthful after launch, including stale/removed records and source outages |

Every selected source story names: user query/use case, expected native item,
content/industry/jurisdiction scope, connector dependency, free-access class,
source-specific acceptance, operating cost and owner. Track **qualified** and
**enabled** separately; a code merge alone does not establish either current
availability or complete catalog coverage.

For public records/maps, include native parcel/document/layer identity, authority,
CRS/extent/scale and date semantics as applicable. For industry guidance, include
occupation/task, model or process, revision and jurisdiction. The
[review template](SOURCE_REVIEW_TEMPLATE.md) already contains these fields.

## 7. Verification and release rules

1. **At qualification:** use the master benchmark and each playbook's specific
   tests. A genuine machine query/import plus usable destination is required;
   documentation and an HTTP 200 alone do not pass.
2. **During implementation:** test the adapter's contract and meaningful failure,
   identity, access and pagination behavior. Use fixtures for outages/429s and
   restricted examples; respect current provider limits for actual source probes.
3. **Before release:** run checks appropriate to the change plus repository release
   requirements, verify an enabled hosted preview and inspect the relevant UI.
   New interaction designs follow their concrete review story. Keep unrelated
   production/account configuration outside source work.
4. **After release:** check the canonical site using actual source requests and
   the declared user journeys. Record exact source SHA, deployment and rollback.
   A failing newly enabled source can be disabled independently when supported;
   otherwise use the prepared release rollback.
5. **Before the next batch:** review freshness, failed-source reports, relevant
   free-limit usage and operating burden. Carry repairs into the next selection
   rather than counting stale sources toward healthy live coverage.

Keep one selected live connector per request initially, signed stateless paging
and bounded local metadata search. Source availability does not require querying
every enabled source every time. No Redis, paid search or new hosted database is
a prerequisite; reconsider infrastructure only for a measured requirement with
a concrete costed alternative.

## 8. Review the program after each cycle

Publish a short batch report, with one row per origin and a summary:

| Measure | What it tells us |
| --- | --- |
| Screened / probed / qualified / enabled / suspended | Where work is accumulating; all are globally deduplicated counts |
| Useful new coverage | New languages, tasks, jurisdictions and successful benchmark cases; item totals only where measured |
| Query and access quality | Known-item recovery, top-result relevance, native/structured-query correctness and working full-item destinations |
| Maintenance and cost | Free-capacity use, upstream calls, refresh effort, stale evidence and failed providers |
| Delivery effort | Time per triage/probe, qualified-to-live elapsed work, connector reuse and causes of delay |
| Breadth | Category/industry matrix and P01–P09 USA/India coverage, with unsampled cells visible |

After two cycles, adjust batch size and capacity using observed qualification and
delivery rates. If fewer than two useful candidates pass a batch, change the
directory/discovery route. If several qualify but remain unshipped, spend the next
cycle on engineering/verification. If freshness failures grow, prioritize repairs
before adding more dependencies. Review sparse categories without inflating
counts or silently dropping the goal.

Do not multiply a daily candidate rate into a promised launch date for 2,000
memberships. The first meaningful milestone is **one repeatable discovery →
qualification → live-release → refresh cycle**, then a second source through the
same process, followed by steady expansion toward the 100-origin milestones.

## 9. Automation after the workflow is proven

Start with on-demand execution and reviewed records. After two successful cycles,
automate deterministic helpers: register deduplication, schema/fixture checks,
coverage reports and bounded source-health/refresh checks consistent with provider
rules. Keep terms judgments, access classification changes and new-source
enablement reviewable.

Any later daily research job needs an explicit schedule, queue, request/time
budget and stop condition. It should propose candidates or draft changes, not
silently label sources qualified or deploy integrations. This plan creates no
recurring task; daily quotas are not needed to begin the first delivery batch.

## 1. Goal and counting rules

The useful outcome is: **a reader searches for something and receives a matching
item, its actual source, and an evidenced free reading/listening/viewing link.**
A list of promising websites is an intermediate research output.

Use 20 research categories: five core areas and 15 additions. Target 100 qualified
sources per category over successive research cycles. These are overlapping
category memberships, potentially 2,000 memberships, not necessarily 2,000 unique
sources or 2,000 custom integrations. Report the global unique count separately.

Add **Industry and job knowledge** as a visible group with 20 industry tags. It is
a second classification axis across those content categories. Track industry
coverage independently and use the same 10 → 25 → 50 → 100 ladder as an eventual
research aspiration for each industry. The same origin may support several
industries and categories; these memberships never add to the global unique count.

Keep four counts separate:

| Count | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Candidate origin | An identified publisher, repository, institution or community with a distinct maintained content catalog; eligibility is unproven. |
| Qualified origin | A candidate whose relevant catalog or explicitly bounded subset passes the queryability, access, permissions and cost gates below. Record the tested scope and date. |
| Enabled origin | A qualified origin actually reachable through a released, tested integration, with current evidence. A source awaiting implementation is not enabled. |
| Connector / index | A machine interface used to reach origins. One aggregator connector can cover multiple evidenced origins; several connectors can cover the same origin. |

Count an origin once globally, and at most once in each relevant category.
Mirrors, language views, formats, feed endpoints, journal titles under one
publisher, and collections under one catalog do not inflate the origin count.
Separately maintained institutional catalogs can qualify independently when their
ownership, identifiers, searchable scope and evidence are recorded. An individual
article, course, podcast episode or PDF is an item, never a source.

For aggregator coverage, record `originId`, `connectorId`, provider attribution
and scope together. An aggregator's advertised institution count is not our
enabled-source count. Each claimed origin needs its own retrieval/access sample;
do not count the aggregator and its member catalogs twice as content origins.

The 100-per-category goal is an ambition to test. Some categories, especially
free audiobooks or children's publishers with reusable catalogs, may have fewer
than 100 suitable independent origins. Record a shortfall and keep the quality
gate; do not pad the count with mirrors or paywalled catalogs.

## 5. Repeatable route to 100 qualified sources in every category

1. **Define the category's boundary and benchmark queries.** Pick five topics,
   five exact known items, relevant languages and two exclusions. Avoid counting
   a generic repository in a category without real examples from that category.
2. **Seed ten candidates per category.** Use the row-specific directories above;
   target four India, four global and two other-region leads. This first pass
   produces up to 200 category memberships, deduplicated into a smaller origin
   register. Add five candidate memberships per industry tag, up to another 100
   memberships, and deduplicate all 300 across the shared origin register. A
   source can satisfy both a content and industry research slot with evidence.
   For civic/maps categories, use the US/India allocation above. Plan up to two
   deep reviews per content category and one per industry, within a maximum of
   **60 unique origins**; the twelve public-records/maps reviews are inside that cap.
   Allocate overlaps first and record any coverage gaps rather than exceed the
   cap to force every suggested slot into the same cycle.
3. **Build an initial pool of 150–250 candidates per category in batches of 25.**
   Expand directory countries/subjects, follow publisher/provider/member links,
   and inspect official institutional sites. This pool size is a planning
   hypothesis, not evidence that those candidates exist or will pass.
4. **Triage each candidate.** In roughly 10–15 minutes identify the operator,
   content scope, rights/access policy, machine route and likely costs. Keep the
   discovery URL and a reason for rejection/deferment. A web search box alone
   passes neither technical nor permission review.
5. **Deep-review the best candidates.** Timebox a first technical/access probe to
   roughly 30–90 minutes; flag unusually complex ones for a separate spike. Use
   the [review template](SOURCE_REVIEW_TEMPLATE.md). Do not write a production
   connector for every candidate during discovery.
6. **Measure conversion after every 25 reviewed candidates.** If the observed
   qualification rate is 40%, 100 qualified origins would require about 250
   reviewed candidates. Use `remaining target / observed pass rate` for the next
   effort estimate; a zero/small sample triggers new discovery routes, not an
   invented success rate. Deduplicate across categories before estimating effort.
7. **Replenish through targeted gaps.** Search underrepresented languages,
   countries, subjects and source types. Example query patterns:

   ```text
   "{category}" "{country}" ("open access" OR "public domain")
   site:{official-institution-domain} (repository OR publications OR digital library)
   "{source name}" (API OR metadata OR OAI-PMH OR OPDS OR export)
   "{native-script category term}" "{state or language}" "{open/free term}"
   "{network name}" (members OR partners OR publishers OR data providers)
   ```

   Inspect search results as leads; never turn search-engine snippets into book
   records or access evidence. Confirm official ownership and lawful distribution.
8. **Close each ladder stage at 10, 25, 50 and 100 qualified origins.** Publish
   counts, gaps, coverage scopes, best next integrations and expiring evidence.
   If repeated discovery routes are exhausted, document the shortfall instead
   of renaming collections to manufacture additional sources.

For hard-to-integrate but valuable origins, prepare a request for a supported
feed or metadata permission. Outreach is a separate action requiring the owner's
instruction; the rest of the research continues without it.

## 6. Queryability and free-access admission gates

A source qualifies only with evidence for **all** of the following:

| Gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Reproducible retrieval | An allowed machine route can retrieve matching item records for the declared category-appropriate query: topic/title, address/parcel/document, geographic extent, or dataset variable/time/geography. It can retrieve or reproduce a specific record using a stable source identifier. Record supported fields and tested scope. |
| Actual item access | At least one usable full item, not only a title/abstract/cover/snippet. Test a representative set, including the destination and any free registration path; per-result access still needs checking. |
| Honest access class | Anonymous and free-account access are eligible and distinct. Free signup does not qualify subscription, institution-only, library-loan, preview or paid-trial content. Geographically limited free sources can qualify for their evidenced audience. |
| Permission and cost | Current terms permit the chosen API/export/index/display use. Metadata reuse and content reading/reuse rights are recorded separately. Identify quotas, key requirements, free limits and paid-overage behavior. |
| Identity and attribution | Stable source/item IDs, title, creator where supplied, content kind, language where supplied, source/host and canonical landing URL. Unknown fields stay unknown. Preserve editions, translations and versions. |
| Maintainable coverage | Defined subset/full-catalog scope, paging or bounded import behavior, refresh/deletion plan and an accountable maintainer. A handpicked record does not establish whole-catalog search. |

Accepted retrieval routes, in preferred order:

1. **Documented live search API**, with record resolution and bounded calls.
2. **Verified aggregator coverage**, with attributable item-level origin/host
   evidence. Confirm known items and missing/lagging coverage per origin; do not
   claim a source's complete catalog simply because it appears in an index.
3. **Official reusable metadata export/feed**, compiled into a bounded local
   search artifact. This is the existing book-catalog approach; it need not add a
   hosted service. Large imports require measured build/memory/refresh costs.
4. **Explicitly permitted structured harvesting**, only where refresh and item
   discovery are sustainable. Document the supported route and its limitations;
   a fragile browser scraper is not the default way to reach 100 sources.

If none passes, keep the source as `deferred: no supported retrieval route`.
A link to search the provider's website may help users, but **does not count as
in-app queryability** or prove that a particular item exists there.

Protocol distinctions matter: [OAI-PMH](https://www.openarchives.org/OAI/openarchivesprotocol.html)
harvests metadata, so it needs an import/search step; [OPDS](https://specs.opds.io/opds-1.2)
describes catalogs and acquisition, with search availability checked per feed.
[MediaWiki search](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Search) and
[CKAN APIs](https://docs.ckan.org/en/latest/api/) offer reusable connector patterns,
but deployed versions, permissions and access vary. RSS can expose only recent
items, sitemaps only URLs, and IIIF only known objects. None automatically proves
full historical keyword search. DOI resolvers help exact lookups, not general
topic search; readable PDFs without discoverable metadata need another route.

## 7. Qualification tests and evidence

Research proof and production acceptance are different stages. For a deep review,
use a small, reproducible probe pack with source-derived expected records:

- Five known items: exact title/ID, author where supported, at least one
  non-English/native-script item when the source claims that coverage. Check
  round-trip search → native record → actual full-item destination.
- Five topic queries chosen before inspecting results. Review top-five results
  for subject match, useful item type and accessible destination. Record
  title/subject/full-text matching limitations. Do not repeat the earlier
  Mathematics problem by accepting unrelated metadata as relevance evidence.
- For public-record/geospatial sources, substitute five appropriate record/spatial
  queries for unsupported keyword searches: jurisdiction + document number,
  address/parcel, map-sheet name, bounding box, or variable + geography + period.
  Test CRS/axis ordering, geographic boundaries, pagination/truncation and survey
  versus publication/effective dates. A documented map viewer alone does not
  establish feature queries, and an API error must never imply no ownership record.
- For industry material, test role/task relevance, applicable country/standard,
  revision date and evidence for each assigned industry tag. A shared regulator
  catalog is one origin even when it spans all twenty industries.
- Negative/gibberish queries, changed filters, punctuation and Unicode. Confirm
  empty results versus source failure. Check a second page or declare the fixed
  import scope; retain duplicates/versions correctly.
- A representative restricted/embargoed/preview item if the catalog contains
  them. Verify exclusion or clear labeling rather than inheriting a blanket
  "free source" assumption. Free-login tests distinguish an advertised offer
  from actually verified post-login access; unavailable proof is a recorded gap.
- Latency, payload size, documented quotas and bounded errors. Test throttling
  and outages with fixtures; do not overload a real service to generate a 429.
- Two independent sessions for shortlisted sources, on different days where
  practical, to detect transient success. Capture timestamp, region, request
  shape, native IDs, policy URLs and a small permitted evidence sample; no keys,
  private cookies or copied full books in evidence.

Suggested pilot acceptance targets, to calibrate before production: all five
known eligible items are found in the declared searchable scope; at least four
of the first five results are relevant on four of five topic queries; no known
restricted item is labeled freely readable. A specialist source can declare
exact-title-only or structured-record/spatial capability, but must not be routed
unsupported queries or counted as general topic-search coverage. A native public
catalog that searches by parcel or document ID can qualify for that declared use.
Identifier redirect services such as DOI resolvers remain supporting services;
they do not themselves establish a searchable content catalog. Small tests establish the declared sample,
not measured recall of the entire catalog. Track these capabilities separately.

Before enabling an origin, add adapter contract/error/access tests, actual source
probes and browser search → detail → outbound action → save → reload checks.
Test phone/desktop, accessibility, all three reading lights, language/region
labels and source selection. Review new UI artifacts first if a new content kind
needs different cards/details; do not force datasets or videos through book UI.

## 8. Scale the integrations without scaling infrastructure prematurely

Keep the research register as reviewed JSON/CSV and Markdown in Git. It is a
source catalog and evidence index, not a new hosted database. Version snapshots
and run bounded local/repository checks within the existing free allowances.

Build shared connector families only when multiple qualified candidates justify
them: native/aggregator JSON search, OAI-PMH imports, CSV/JSON/MARC exports, OPDS,
MediaWiki, repository APIs and later dataset/media/geospatial interfaces. Evaluate
documented OGC/ArcGIS services with explicit catalog, map-view and feature-query
capabilities; do not assume every deployment supports the same operations. Reuse transport and
tests while retaining per-source mappings, policies and access rules. DSpace,
EPrints or OJS software alone is not proof that a site's interface is enabled.

**100 sources available does not mean 100 network calls per search.** Keep one
selected live connector per request initially, with source switching. Prefer an
eligible broad index when it supplies useful attributable coverage; route more
specialist searches by category, language and declared capabilities. A source
registry suggests where to search; it cannot assert that an unqueried source
contains the requested title. Only retrieved item evidence supports that claim.

Future routing should be deterministic first. Show which connector/origins were
searched, bounded catalog coverage, exclusions and failures. An explicit choice
must not silently search something else. Search more sources on reader request;
any later small parallel-search design needs its own latency, cost and pagination
proof. No paid LLM routing, vector database or blanket fan-out is prerequisite.

This trades exhaustive live coverage for bounded cost and responsiveness. A
qualified source can be available through explicit selection without being queried
on every search; report that distinction. For imported metadata, one local query
can search multiple origins within the declared snapshot. As imports grow,
evaluate bounded category/language artifacts against actual hosting limits before
adding more state or promising an all-source search.

Measure search latency, upstream calls, memory/build size, refresh effort and
free-limit usage during the pilot. Revisit infrastructure only for an observed
limit or a source's mandatory coordination requirement, with a specific costed
design. Free upstream APIs still consume existing hosting and maintenance time.

Refresh operational health and access evidence separately from long-term source
policy reviews. Use each source's documented limits/change cadence; monthly
directory gap reviews and periodic policy checks are planning defaults, not a
reason to hammer every endpoint daily. Suspend failing source actions honestly.
Current reading-evidence expiry rules remain in force unless explicitly revised
with evidence; source expansion does not renew stale StoryWeaver observations.

## 9. Delivery milestones and stories

Expand engineering tasks only when each story is reached. This plan creates a
bounded first research cycle; it does not create thousands of speculative tasks.

| Milestone / story | Deliverable | Exit condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M0: Taxonomy and research contract | Accepted content categories, twenty industry tags, six detailed playbooks, count rules and review template | Current revision incorporates owner direction on industries and US/India civic/maps coverage; implementation remains future work |
| M1: Candidate register and first survey | Ten leads/content category plus five/industry; shared deduplicated register and country/language/occupation gaps | Up to 300 category/industry memberships; actual unique count and P01–P09 USA/India coverage reported |

M1–M2 are an initial multi-week research effort for one implementer, not an

effort/free capacity (20%). Treat these as planning weights, calibrated after the
pilot; failing a mandatory gate cannot be rescued by a high score. Compare against
the current sources to avoid spending a sprint on mostly duplicate holdings.

## FCD01: contract decisions

- Content keys use `fcd:v1:<source>:<record>`; Gutenberg records are positive
  integer IDs; Europe PMC records include their source (`MED`, `PMC`, `PPR`).
  A DOI is an identifier, never an app key. Versions, translations, chapters and
  recordings retain distinct source-native keys. No fuzzy-title merge.
- Reviewed StoryWeaver translations use distinct native story IDs. The pilot
  requires English/Hindi/Tamil records with original credits, publisher levels
  and per-record review evidence before enablement.
- An omitted `kinds` searches books/learning resources. Paper searches supply
  paper kinds explicitly. Mixed book/paper requests are reported unsupported;
  the API never silently omits one requested scope.
- Search and resolve both accept `country` (ISO alpha-2 or absent/unknown) and
  language context. An observation for one explicit country does not establish
  availability in another. Gutenberg's US rights statement is retained with a
  generic country-rules prompt, not turned into a global legal claim.
- A reading action requires an explicit per-location `free_full_text` claim,
  positive evidence field/source/time, a safe supplied HTTP(S) URL, and an
  observation no older than 24 hours. Stale, missing, contradictory or
  country-mismatched observations become unknown; fetch failure is not absence.
  Reuse licence and free reading remain distinct. Missing licence never becomes
  an invented Creative Commons licence.
- `not_selected` means the planner did not query this source; `disabled` means
  it is not connected. `ok` with zero results is distinct from timeout,
  unavailable, throttled and quota-exhausted. Counts describe loaded items,
  never a federated global total.
- Default results contain anonymous free full text and a separately labelled verified free-account group (owner clarification 2026-11-01). An explicit unclear group may
  contain unknown/metadata-only items with labelled source links; previews,
  borrowing, unknown-price registration and restricted access stay excluded in v1.
- Source cursors remain server-owned. Browser tokens bind query, context,
  policy/index revisions and expiry. Shared live quota reservation and page
  advancement must pass a two-instance test before a live source is enabled.
  A memory implementation is a development/test adapter only; store failure
  disables uncapped live dispatch while keeping local metadata searchable.

## Browser shelf decision (before FCD04 implementation)

Persist a version-2 object with existing `savedBooks`/`recentBooks` untouched and
an additional `savedContent` array. Each content entry has
`kind: 'content'`, `contentKey`, `itemKind`, `title`, `authors`, optional safe
cover/host label and `savedAt`. No fake `bookKey` or ISBN; it opens
`/app/read/:contentKey`, never a library circulation route.

Read version 1 without rewriting it; on the first successful write, migrate to
version 2 under the same browser-storage key. Retain all existing saved books,
library choice and history; corrupt data keeps the existing recovery path.
Preserve the original object if migration write fails. Library books and content
share the existing 100-item save cap. Papers use the existing typeset-cover
fallback, labelled by item kind. Shelf sort operates on title/authors/saved time;
content never triggers a library availability check. Clear saved books clears
both saved collections after confirmation; viewed library history is unchanged.
Future account sync can carry this tagged content reference without merging it
into book-edition identity. No account feature is part of this delivery.

Canonical repository: **[ddk220-light/MyBookshelf-web](https://github.com/ddk220-light/MyBookshelf-web)**. All future development belongs here.

Build a **metadata discovery service with outbound reading links**. Use a hybrid of locally indexed metadata catalogs and a small number of live search adapters. The app should not download or serve the books or papers themselves.

This is feasible with free sources. The difficult parts are deciding whether a specific edition is actually readable, keeping source permissions and quotas current, and combining overlapping records without losing versions or translations. Free content does not imply an unlimited free search API.

- [Source catalog](source-catalog.md): categories, repositories, connection methods, credentials, constraints, and priorities.
- [Architecture and delivery plan](architecture.md): contracts, query flow, storage, repository integration, and rollout gates.
- [Evidence](evidence.json): historical request URLs, observed outcomes, selected findings, and verification limits.

## Recommendation

Start with **Free books** and **Research papers**. Add **Textbooks & learning** through the Open Textbook Library catalog, then a curated **Children's books** collection. Treat language, subject, reading level, format, and access conditions as separate filters rather than mutually exclusive categories.

| First integrations | Connection | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project Gutenberg | Official metadata import; local search | Public-domain ebook foundation without scraping or dependence on the public Gutendex demo |
| Open Textbook Library | Official CSV/JSON metadata; local search | Documented CC0 catalog for educational material |
| DOAJ | Live article search | OA journal articles with publisher full-text links |
| Europe PMC | Live search and record details | Biomedical literature with explicit full-text/OA fields |
| arXiv | Atom API behind a shared request queue | Direct preprint coverage with clearly labeled versions |
| OpenAlex | Live search after key/budget verification | Broad multidisciplinary discovery and OA locations; usage is metered |
| DOAB / OAPEN | Metadata imports and OAI-PMH updates | Scholarly books and chapters; next import candidates |

Reuse Google Books and Open Library selectively to enrich book records and resolve existing saved books to candidate free editions. Their general catalogs contain previews, borrowing offers, and metadata-only records; they should not define the free-reading collection by themselves.

## Categories

| Category | Typical material | Representative sources |
| --- | --- | --- |
| General ebooks and public-domain literature | Novels, poetry, essays, historical nonfiction | Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks, Wikisource, Internet Archive |
| Scholarly books and chapters | Research monographs, edited volumes, academic chapters | DOAB, OAPEN |
| Journal articles | Published research and reviews | DOAJ, Europe PMC/PMC, OpenAlex |
| Preprints and working papers | Research before or outside formal journal publication | arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv, HAL, Zenodo |
| Theses, dissertations, institutional outputs | Graduate research, technical reports, repository manuscripts | CORE, HAL, Shodhganga, university repositories |
| Textbooks and open educational resources | Textbooks, lessons, course readings, exercises | Open Textbook Library, OpenStax, LibreTexts, OER Commons, NCERT, DIKSHA |
| Children's books and early literacy | Picture books, graded stories, translations, wordless books | StoryWeaver, African Storybook, Book Dash |
| Government, policy, organizational publications | Reports, policy papers, public documents | World Bank Open Knowledge Repository, Library of Congress, institutional repositories |
| Historical and cultural collections | Digitized books, serials, rare texts, regional-language literature | Internet Archive, Library of Congress, Europeana, Biodiversity Heritage Library, Wikisource |
| Audiobooks (optional extension) | Recorded readings of public-domain books | LibriVox |

Journals are **containers**, articles are **items**, and PDF/EPUB/HTML are **formats**. Children's and educational are audience/use classifications that can apply to several item types. An ebook can be a textbook, a children's story, or an academic monograph simultaneously.

## What the original checks established

Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.

These were small one-time checks, not integration, rights, uptime, completeness, or user-country tests. Important counterexamples:

- An Open Library work returned `ebook_access: public` alongside many Internet Archive identifiers. That does not identify which edition is freely readable.
- A HAL hit had a record URL and DOI but no `fileMain_s`: a repository hit is not necessarily full text.
- Zenodo returned a dataset; item-type filtering is essential.
- DOAJ supplied an older HTTP publisher URL; metadata alone does not prove the destination still works.
- Semantic Scholar returned **429**, and Gutendex timed out. Those checks do not establish general service availability.
- Some documentation URLs moved; corrected DOAB/OAPEN URLs appear in the catalog. Some sites returned only a JavaScript shell. NCERT/ERIC/OER Commons could not be fully inspected.

Two current details make older integration advice unreliable: Standard Ebooks' full OPDS feeds require membership/access arrangements, and Unpaywall's documentation said its title-search endpoint retired on **2026-09-18**. Use Unpaywall for DOI resolution and another index for search. Recheck these policies before implementation.

# Free-book relevance and disabled paper search

Owner report and task: [#154](https://github.com/ddk220-light/MyBookshelf-web/issues/154),
2026-11-01. Worktree: `/workspace/MyBookshelf-web-free-sources-implementation`,
branch `research/free-content-discovery-relevance`, based on production main
`1c16815`. The owner clarified that free-book requests succeed but return poorly
ranked results. This is separate from the deferred paper connection.

## Reproduced behavior

The production API returned 20 results for `Mathematics`. Search treated title,
contributors and subjects as one substring field, then sorted all non-exact-title
matches alphabetically. Thus a psychology/statistics title with a broad supplied
Mathematics subject preceded a book with Mathematics in its title. Short terms
could also match inside unrelated words.

| Position | Previous first page | Revised first page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A Computational Introduction to Number Theory and Algebra | Contemporary Mathematics |
| 2 | A Contemporary Approach to Research and Statistics in Psychology | Advanced Water Mathematics |
| 3 | A Cool Brisk Walk Through Discrete Mathematics - version 2.2 | Applied Finite Mathematics |
| 4 | A First Course in Linear Algebra | Fundamentals of Mathematics |
| 5 | A First Course in Linear Algebra - 10th Edition-2023-B-D | MGF 1131: Mathematics in Context |

The revised first 20 results all contain Mathematics in their titles. This is a
metadata relevance improvement, not a claim about the best textbook for a
reader's level or a larger catalog. Genuine subject-only matches remain available
after closer matches and show `Subject: …` using the source's own metadata.

## Change

Local search ranks exact titles, complete title phrases/words, contributor
matches and supplied subjects. All query terms must match. Word boundaries
exclude matches such as AI inside chair and art inside cartography or artificial;
prefix matching is available for terms of at least four characters. Latin accent
folding and Indic vowel signs remain intact. Source editions are not merged.

Each result may carry an optional query-scoped `searchMatch` with a field and
source value. Resolve and saved-reference contracts do not change. The local
index revision includes the ranking revision so cursors issued under the previous
ordering restart instead of silently skipping or repeating records.

When the paper sources are disabled, the UI now says **Paper search isn’t enabled
yet**, offers **Search free books instead** with the same query, and does not
offer a retry or depict a network outage. Explicit paper IDs and source-only
requests also report disabled before attempting shared coordination. Genuine
timeouts/outages retain retry and the warning that failure does not prove absence.

# Simple free live discovery

Owner direction, 2026-11-03 (America/Los_Angeles): avoid a data store until a
specific requirement demonstrates its need. Current traffic is negligible.
This plan supersedes the shared Redis/cache/session architecture for the initial
paper release. Track [FCD10 #156](https://github.com/ddk220-light/MyBookshelf-web/issues/156).

## Product requirements

- Search one selected paper source live. General searches use OpenAlex;
  biomedical searches and PMCIDs use Europe PMC. The Sources sheet switches
  sources. Explicit selection never silently searches a different source.
- Show more carries the provider's paging token in a signed browser token.
  Opening a result resolves its native record directly at that provider.
- No new database, Redis account, paid integration, shared cache or stored search
  session. Existing account features/resources are outside this change.
- Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays off because its aggregate pacing rules need
  coordination across deployments. Offer searches on their source websites;
  these connectors do not block other paper sources.
- Keep current source identities, verified free-reading rules, credits, versions,
  separate translations, source errors and browser shelf behavior.

## Engineering design

One supported adapter is called per request, with bounded deadlines/response
sizes and no automatic retry/fan-out. OpenAlex also checks its free allowance
before its search or exact-record request. Client disconnects cancel work.

Signed cursors contain provider, native paging token, query/context hash, fixed
15-minute expiry and bounded recent-cursor history. They contain no API key,
result records or server-side session pointer. Query/type/access/language/source
changes, tampering, old shared-session cursors and expiry require a fresh search.
Provider URLs remain fixed inside adapters.

Each replay makes a live request. Upstream indexes can change between pages:
this version does not promise a frozen snapshot or global duplicate-free paging.
Deduplicate source keys within each page and loaded browser results. There are no
excess merged records to buffer. A page may be underfilled when some upstream
records fail kind/access checks, while still offering the next provider page.

Only verified free locations produce reading actions. Missing, stale or
contradictory evidence remains unclear. Failures never mean no free copy.

## Cost and limits

Europe PMC uses its public API. OpenAlex uses the existing server-only key;
verify its free allowance, accepted endpoint pricing and zero prepaid balance
before dispatch. Exhaustion, paid balances or unknown policy stop the request.
No paid fallback or paid infrastructure is introduced. Normal hosting usage
continues under the existing Vercel plan; future hosting costs are not guaranteed
to be zero.

Provider-side throttles are authoritative. Honor retry-after information and
show outages/limits distinctly. This profile makes no application-wide daily
quota guarantee. Request count, payload size, deadline and continuation depth
remain bounded without a database.

## Configuration and delivery

Keep the existing discovery flag and strong cursor signer. Enable Europe PMC
and optionally OpenAlex with its key. Remove Redis and per-source application
daily/minute budget variables from active setup. No client-exposed credentials
or database migration.

1. Revise plan/operations and supersede the blanket Redis gate (#86).
2. Implement direct search/detail requests and signed provider paging; remove
   obsolete Redis runtime/test scaffolding.
3. Adapt source selection, outbound source searches and coverage messaging.
4. Verify routing, cost guards, cursor tampering/restarts, errors/access,
   reading/saving, accessibility and real hosted flows, then release checked main.

Reconsider shared infrastructure only for a demonstrated requirement: an
aggregate-paced connector, measured traffic exceeding provider/hosting limits,
or a deliberate need for frozen merged search sessions. Document that requirement
and costs before selecting or provisioning a store.
