# Free-content discovery architecture

**Current decision (2026-11-03):** the owner requested the
[simple free live plan](SIMPLE_LIVE_PLAN.md). One source is queried live per
request, with signed provider paging and no data-store prerequisite. That plan
supersedes the shared cache/quota/session design below, which is retained as
historical scaling research rather than a launch requirement.

Implementation update (2026-11-01): the delivered bounded catalogs use bundled,
read-only metadata and local search; PostgreSQL is not a prerequisite for this
release. Shared Redis coordinates live paper sources. The owner has accepted
verified free source accounts, represented separately as `free_account_required`.
See [current contracts/progress](IMPLEMENTATION.md), [source operations](OPERATIONS.md)
and [the reviewed children's set](CHILDREN_REVIEW.md). The scale architecture below
remains planning guidance where it differs from those implemented choices.

Proposed design, originally researched 2026-10-31 and reconstructed for the canonical MyBookshelf-web repository. Scope: search metadata and link users to content at its existing host. No connectors, migrations or runtime changes are implemented by this branch.

## 1. System shape

Use a **hybrid search service**: index small explicitly redistributable catalogs locally; federate selected APIs for large/fast-moving collections; resolve identifiers and access links on demand. Keep the existing React/Express stack.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U[React search and item details] --> API[Express content API]
    API --> P[Query planner and access filters]
    P --> I[Local metadata search]
    P --> F[Bounded live adapters]
    P --> R[DOI and edition resolvers]
    F --> C[Shared cache and provider budgets]
    R --> C
    C --> S[External search APIs]
    I --> N[Normalize, reconcile and rank]
    F --> N
    R --> N
    N --> U
    U -->|Read at source| H[Original content host]
    B[Scheduled metadata imports] --> D[Staging records and provenance]
    D --> I
    M[Provider manifests and policy] --> P
    M --> B
```

Reading traffic goes directly from browser to host. The server handles metadata, not PDF/EPUB proxying. Embedding is unnecessary initially and many hosts disallow framing.

| Approach | Benefits | Costs / failures | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Live-only federation | Little storage; fresh upstream search | Quotas, latency, incompatible paging, dependencies on every query | Use for a few large indexes |
| Index everything | Predictable ranking/filtering | Huge imports, rights, freshness, infrastructure | Avoid broad scholarly database imports initially |
| Hybrid | Independent catalog search plus specialist coverage | Two ingestion paths, provenance reconciliation | Recommended |

A modular service is enough; providers are modules, not microservices. A separate scheduled process/job can use the same normalization code.

## 2. Fit with the current repository

Canonical base for this transfer: `9f5bb4b` in `ddk220-light/MyBookshelf-web`. React lives in `client/`, anonymous Express `/api/v2` in `server/`. Current app routes use `/app/`. Existing caches/rate limits are process-local and shelves are browser data. Account persistence is separately planned, not implemented. Coordinate shared persistence decisions with that plan rather than introducing a competing book identity system.

| Existing area | Proposed work |
| --- | --- |
| `server/public-v2/router.js`, `validation.js`, `contracts.js` | Add content-specific search/resolve validation and responses. Do not map all scholarly errors to library catalog failures. |
| `server/public-v2/metadata.js`, `server/services/bookMetadata.js` | Retain exact ISBN/Open Library/Google identity behavior. Free-reading access is new evidence, not circulation availability. Factor only genuinely shared request code. |
| `server/services/providers/` | Keep library adapters separate. New `server/services/content/` must not require branch holdings, patrons, loans, holds or circulation `checkAvailability`. |
| `server/services/providers/http.js` | Reuse timeout/cache/queue concepts after checking suitability. Current maps cannot enforce quotas across Vercel instances. |
| `client/src/v2/ui/scan/`, `ui/book/` | Add Free books / Research scopes and content details. Papers need bibliographic cards without mandatory covers/ISBNs. |
| [Work-aware search](../../work-aware-search.md) | Preserve explicit work/edition relationships and the rule that fuzzy titles do not prove identity. |

Proposed modules:

```text
server/services/content/
  registry.js       # source capabilities, permissions, budgets, mappings
  search.js         # planning, fan-out, ranking and paging
  normalize.js      # identifiers, records, relations, provenance
  access.js         # eligibility and outbound reading actions
  adapters/         # source/protocol adapters
  imports/          # metadata ingestion and checkpoints
server/public-v2/content.js
client/src/v2/ui/content/
```

Do not add global indexes to the geographic library directory. Preserve existing ISBN/work/catalog keys; introduce content keys independently. Adding papers to shelves needs an explicit later storage decision. The outbound-link MVP needs no shelf migration. Current Vercel requests must not depend on writable local disk or SQLite.

## 3. Canonical model

Separate **conceptual work**, **edition/version**, **source record**, and **access location**. A flat `Book { isbn, pdfUrl }` cannot represent translations, preprints, chapters and multiple hosts.

Proposed contract sketch, not production code:

```ts
type Item = {
  key: string; // stable opaque app key, not a temporary URL
  kind: 'book' | 'chapter' | 'article' | 'preprint' | 'thesis'
      | 'report' | 'learning_resource' | 'audiobook' | 'other';
  title: string;
  contributors: Array<{ name: string; role: string; orcid?: string }>;
  identifiers: Array<{ scheme: string; value: string }>;
  languages: string[]; // normalized BCP-47 where possible; retain original value
  subjects: string[];
  audience?: { label?: string; readingLevel?: string; sourceId: string };
  publishedAt?: string;
  version?: string;
  container?: { title: string; issn?: string; volume?: string; issue?: string };
  relations: Array<{ kind: string; targetKey: string; evidence: string }>;
  locations: AccessLocation[];
  provenance: Array<{
    sourceId: string; sourceRecordId: string; recordUrl: string;
    retrievedAt: string; modifiedAt?: string; mappingVersion: string;
  }>;
};

type AccessLocation = {
  id: string;
  landingUrl: string;
  readerUrl?: string;
  downloads: Array<{ url: string; mimeType: string }>;
  access: 'free_full_text' | 'free_account_required' | 'preview' | 'borrow' | 'registration'
        | 'restricted' | 'metadata_only' | 'unknown';
  license?: { id?: string; url?: string; statement?: string };
  rightsJurisdiction?: string;
  country?: string; // applies to this observation, when known
  version?: 'submitted' | 'accepted' | 'published' | 'other';
  evidence: { sourceId: string; field: string; observedAt: string };
  linkCheck?: { checkedAt: string; outcome: 'reachable' | 'broken' | 'unknown' };
};
```

Free full text is an access claim, not reuse permission. HTTP 200 is not free-reading evidence: login pages can return 200. Preserve field-level provenance when choosing conflicting titles/languages/licenses/URLs. Abstracts/covers are optional and must respect source display/storage terms. Journal browsing would use a separate Container entity, not a fake readable item. Exclude datasets/software unless their categories are explicitly enabled.

Identity rules:

1. Normalize exact DOI, ISBN-10/13 equivalence, PMID/PMCID and provider IDs. Valid DOI syntax does not establish existence.
2. Reconcile descriptions of the same identified version, retaining all locations and provenance. Conflicting authoritative metadata goes to review.
3. Keep translations, editions, chapters, abridgements and recordings separate. ISBN is edition-level; ISSN container-level. Missing ISBN is valid.
4. Preserve arXiv versions and Zenodo version DOI separately from concept/unversioned identifiers. Preprint and journal article can be related without being identical. Relations require source evidence.
5. Use title/author similarity only for candidate review or visual grouping, never authoritative merging.
6. Assign durable app IDs to persisted records; alias older source-native keys rather than breaking links after reconciliation.

## 4. Source registry and adapters

Each manifest declares source name/role, official docs/review date, supported item kinds/languages/query fields/filters/sorting, exact-ID resolution, paging/harvesting, credential references, full-text evidence mapping, allowed origins, attribution and metadata reuse policy. Include global rate/concurrency/daily-budget limits, timeouts/cache policy, jurisdiction caveats, source owner, last contract check and feature flag.

Use explicit evidence status: `live_sample`, `docs_only`, `partner_required`, `blocked_check`. A successful old sample is not permission to enable a provider before current requirements are met.

```ts
interface ContentSource {
  search?(request: ProviderQuery, context: RequestContext): Promise<ProviderPage>;
  resolve?(sourceRecordId: string, context: RequestContext): Promise<SourceRecord>;
  locate?(identifier: Identifier, context: RequestContext): Promise<AccessLocation[]>;
  harvest?(checkpoint: Checkpoint, context: JobContext): AsyncIterable<HarvestPage>;
}
```

`ProviderPage` carries mapped records, opaque source cursor, status/warnings and optional source-local total with semantics. Context includes deadline/abort signal, contact, credential accessor and shared budget client. Escape each provider's query grammar; do not send user text as arbitrary Solr/OAI syntax.

Unpaywall implements `locate`, not search. Crossref enriches bibliography. OAI implements `harvest` and feeds a local-index search adapter. Unsupported filters must be rejected or disclosed, never silently ignored while presenting supposedly filtered results.

## 5. Search and item resolution

Proposed POST routes match the existing API style:

```text
POST /api/v2/content/search
  { query, kinds?, languages?, access: "free_full_text", country?, cursor?, limit? }
POST /api/v2/content/resolve
  { key }
```

1. Validate query length, filters, page size (initial max 40), country and cursor binding. Detect ISBN/DOI/arXiv/PMCID before broad search. Country is access context, not legal assurance.
2. Choose providers by user scope/capabilities. Books start from local catalogs; papers use OpenAlex when configured plus at most two relevant specialists. Without the broad index, disclose narrower DOAJ/Europe PMC/arXiv coverage.
3. Use shared cached results. Acquire global quota tokens for uncached requests; arXiv pacing includes all replicas/jobs. Skip with explicit status if the queue cannot run before the deadline.
4. Bound fan-out: proposed 5-second total search deadline, shorter per-provider limits where feasible, at most 3 live providers and one source page each. These are design targets, not measured guarantees. Busy arXiv queues cannot delay every result indefinitely.
5. Map, filter, reconcile and rank. Avoid detail requests for every hit; resolve uncertain access for bounded visible candidates or on item open. Unknown candidates cannot be advertised as free.
6. Return items, source statuses and freshness. Empty, timeout, throttled, quota-exhausted, unsupported and disabled differ. If all sources fail with no local/cached result, return retriable unavailable, not zero matches.
7. On item open, enrich locations as needed; surface editions/versions and host actions. Cache bibliography separately from access observations.

Example partial response:

```json
{
  "items": [],
  "nextCursor": null,
  "coverage": "partial",
  "sources": [
    { "id": "doaj", "status": "ok", "returned": 0 },
    { "id": "arxiv", "status": "timeout", "retryable": true }
  ]
}
```

### Ranking and paging

Use lexical relevance, title/author exactness, identifier matches, requested language and access evidence. Reciprocal-rank fusion can combine incomparable provider scores. Citation/download counts are not default quality judgments. Show source-supplied preprint/retracted/corrected status without implying independent verification.

Federation cannot promise a global total or globally newest-first order without sufficient indexing. Show loaded counts and source coverage. Restrict global sort to fully indexed scopes or explain/reject unsupported sorting.

Keep a short-lived server-side search session in shared cache: query/filter hash, selected sources, provider cursors, buffered unused records, emitted IDs, exhaustion/failure state and index revision. Return a signed opaque token with initial 15-minute expiry. This prevents skipped buffered results, duplicate pages and credential leaks. Preserve order within a session; failed sources retain retry state rather than becoming exhausted. Expiry starts a new query without deleting displayed results.

### Reading actions

Prefer durable supplied landing/reader URLs over guessed PDF paths or signed URLs. Labels must accurately distinguish Read at host, Download EPUB/PDF, Preview, Borrow and View source record. Exclude unknown access by default from Read free; optional broader discovery can show it explicitly.

Show index and host separately when useful, e.g. Found via DOAJ / Read at publisher. Preserve required attribution. Broken PDF links should fall back to evidenced landing/alternate locations, never invented files. Expose freshness/country limits in details. A public-domain US scan is not a universal legal-access assertion.

## 6. Persistence, refresh and operations

Use managed PostgreSQL for the bounded local catalogs, identifiers, relations, locations, source policies and harvest checkpoints. Coordinate with planned account persistence; this is not approval for migrations or a universal catalog. PostgreSQL full-text search can serve initial catalogs; add a specialized engine only when size, typo tolerance or multilingual needs justify it. Test Tamil/Indic and other non-Latin queries; English stemming is not multilingual search.

Use Redis or equivalent atomic shared KV for search cache, coalescing, sessions, circuit breakers and source rate/daily budgets. Memory-only implementations can support local development, not cross-instance production limits. Object storage is optional for permitted metadata snapshots; do not store raw copyrighted text by default. No writable local disk/SQLite dependency in Vercel request paths.

A reviewed static metadata snapshot/in-process search is a smaller initial option if bundle/memory measurements permit. It still needs shared live-provider budgeting. Provision no paid infrastructure as a side effect of a connector.

Proposed defaults, always subordinate to provider terms:

| Data | Initial freshness | Failure behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live query | 15-minute cache; stale fallback up to 24 hours | Explicit stale/partial, bounded lifetime |
| Bibliography | 1–7 days by provider | Retain source/time |
| Access evidence | Re-evaluate on open when older than 24 hours | Downgrade unknown/conflicting evidence |
| Imports | Daily checks when supported; monthly dumps on their schedule | Retain last successful index and show age |
| Negative lookup | Short cache, e.g. 5 minutes | Never cache an error as absence |
| Links | Sampled/background and on-open checks | 403/anti-bot means unknown, not automatic deletion |

Import sequence: approved metadata fetch → size/schema/revision validation → normalized staging → count/deletion sanity checks → reconciliation → atomic index activation. Commit OAI pages before checkpointing. Use overlapping datestamp windows, idempotent upserts, tombstones and periodic reconciliation. Granularity/deletion support vary. Expired resumption tokens restart safely from durable windows. Failed/empty snapshots must never wipe the catalog.

Honor Retry-After; jittered exponential backoff within deadlines; stop retrying missing-permission 401/403 indefinitely. Quota exhaustion returns local/cached coverage plus status. Disable one source via flag without taking down discovery.

Measure per-source requests/cache hits/latency/timeouts/429s/budget, usable free-link rate, missing evidence, duplicates, cursor errors, harvest lag/deletions and sampled broken links. Avoid raw query logs by default; aggregate operations suffice initially.

## 7. Rights and network boundaries

Keep separate: permission to ingest/display metadata, ability to read content, and permission to reuse content. CC0 metadata does not make PDFs CC0. Public-domain status depends on jurisdiction; free copyrighted reading can still prohibit redistribution.

Only approved adapters make server requests. Validate source next-page URLs/cursors against expected origins/paths; escape queries and sanitize metadata HTML. Allow web schemes for displayed outbound links. A server-side link checker must reject private/reserved addresses and revalidate DNS/redirects to avoid SSRF. Never turn user-supplied URLs into arbitrary server fetches. Keep credentials out of logs, client variables and public URLs; do not persist signed downloads as identity or fixtures.

No cross-site cookies, account creation, login replay or paywall bypass is needed. Handle removals, embargoes, retractions and policy changes through source updates/removal mechanisms.

## 8. Delivery and acceptance

### Phase A — contract and two vertical slices

Define manifests/model/access eligibility/shared budgeting/routes. Implement Gutenberg import/local search and Europe PMC live search to prove both paths. Add cards/details/host actions behind a flag and sanitized fixtures under source terms.

Exit: book/paper queries lead to real host links; preview/borrow/metadata-only fixtures cannot enter the free filter; one failure retains other results; no dependence on a public demo or writable local disk.

### Phase B — initial coverage

Add Open Textbook Library, DOAJ and arXiv; OpenAlex after key/budget verification. Then DOAB/OAPEN imports and optional Unpaywall resolver with real contact email. Keep Google/Open Library enrichment bounded.

Exit: DOI duplicates consolidate without collapsing versions/chapters/translations; paging retains buffered items; quotas work across two instances; failed refresh cannot delete active index.

### Phase C — children, regional and specialist coverage

Reviewed children's pilot with approved metadata, attribution, language and level. Obtain feeds for comprehensive StoryWeaver/African Storybook/Book Dash search. Add CORE/HAL/Zenodo and India-specific providers in response to measured gaps; audio optional.

Exit: every enabled provider has ingestion permission, refresh owner, stable link mapping and tested access policy. Partner-pending/catalog-only coverage stays explicitly scoped.

Before release verify:

- Provider contracts: valid/empty/malformed response, missing fields, absent license, preview/borrow/embargo, stale links, 429/503 and schema drift.
- Identity: same DOI across indexes, preprint vs publication, arXiv versions, translations, chapter vs book, missing ISBN, unrelated same title, Zenodo concept vs version DOI.
- Search: partial/all-source failure, exhausted budget, unsupported filters, cancellation, no skipped/duplicate pages, expired cursor, honest totals.
- Imports: interrupted/repeated OAI page, tombstone, expired token, corrupt/empty bulk file and rollback.
- End-to-end: title/author/DOI, free filters, details, external HTML/reader/PDF/EPUB where offered, browser back, unchanged ISBN/library/shelf flows; launch-country checks beyond server-region behavior.
- Capacity: uncached searches/day and peak concurrency. At the observed OpenAlex price, ordinary search cost is uncached calls × $0.001; paging/enrichment add requests. arXiv 1/3 sec is at most 20/min before contention. Configure degradation before enabling traffic.

This documentation-only branch needs document/link/JSON checks, not runtime tests. Implementation should run server/client suites, typecheck/build, targeted connector/import tests and opt-in live smoke checks; unit tests should not depend on networking.

## 9. Inputs still needed for implementation

Verify the configured OpenAlex key with an actual authenticated request and select a real application contact email. Decide expected traffic and commercial/noncommercial use before setting quotas and eligibility. Choose initial children's languages/levels and launch countries before feeds and access validation. No missing input blocks this research or its publication; the proposal itself authorizes no new paid resources or accounts.

# G01 first ten: query-verified source candidates

Research date: **2026-11-05 UTC**. Owner request: identify and share ten strong
queryable sources; **do not add them to the app**.
Backlog [#164](https://github.com/ddk220-light/MyBookshelf-web/issues/164);
active group [#165](https://github.com/ddk220-light/MyBookshelf-web/issues/165).

## Result and evidence boundary

Ten recommended source candidates returned actual machine-search results without
an API key or reader account in this review. Representative reading destinations
also exposed text, PDF bytes or audio bytes. The evidence is in
[G01_QUERY_EVIDENCE.json](G01_QUERY_EVIDENCE.json), including request parameters,
publisher IDs, native item IDs, UTC observations, small metadata samples and
response hashes. Supporting access and negative/paging observations are in
[G01_ACCESS_EVIDENCE.json](G01_ACCESS_EVIDENCE.json).

Status is **probed / recommended for owner review**, not production-qualified or
enabled. The full five-known-item/five-topic benchmark, repeated-session
reliability, accessibility/browser journeys and country-specific rights/access
checks remain later qualification tasks. Byte-range PDF/audio checks establish
anonymous retrieval of the sampled files; they do not certify every page or a
complete listening experience. No adapter, runtime manifest, source flag, catalog
import, deployment, database, scheduled task or source account was added.

## The ten candidates

Five publishers share **one** documented [Thoth API](https://thoth.pub/docs).
Thoth is a connector, not an eleventh content origin.
Its [metadata policy](https://thoth.pub/docs/policies/terms-thoth-metadata)
permits public access and CC0 metadata reuse. Book licenses remain independent.

This is ten discovery options, not ten demonstrated net-new origins in production.
GDL and BHL aggregate contributors; do not add their contributor counts on top.
BHL's Internet Archive hosting is not another source. Measure item/publisher
overlap with existing StoryWeaver, Book Dash, OTL and Gutenberg before reporting
incremental coverage. The five named publishers have distinct publisher IDs;
their chapters, editions and mirrored files do not increase that count.

| GDL | English **Rain** page exposed 15 H5P chapter/page units; Hindi sample exposed 19, without login. Per-book CC licenses differ. The `rain` result set also included **Queens of Shakrain**, so native substring search needs relevance checks. Avoid double-counting StoryWeaver/other republished stories. |

Native page IDs and parent/section links resolved. | Search returns chapters, version pages and entire works together. | Library of Congress | Sample item declared unrestricted access and public-domain reuse; its PDF returned HTTP 206 and PDF bytes. | API covers digital collections rather than the whole library catalog. Keep per-item rights, scan/OCR quality and historical publication date. Metadata result alone is insufficient. |
| BHL | Exact matched item supplied institutional attribution, a public-domain statement and a public PDF; PDF returned HTTP 206 and PDF bytes. | Scope this route to BHL's maintained collection and retain contributing-library attribution. Members may overlap other catalogs. Historical taxonomy/terminology and volume identities matter; modern in-copyright items require their own licenses. |
| LibriVox | API returned 12 sections for recording 200. First, middle and final section URLs returned HTTP 206 audio/mpeg bytes. | Other results included a different recording and an abridged version. Preserve narrator, recording ID, language and abridgement. US public-domain statements do not establish worldwide rights. |
| African Minds | Publisher-attributed record contained a CC BY 4.0 license and a canonical PDF that returned HTTP 206/PDF bytes. | Tested subset only; preserve volume identity and per-title licenses. |
| LSE Press | Sample **Afghanistan** record had CC BY 4.0 and a canonical PDF returning HTTP 206/PDF bytes. | Other titles have other CC terms. Select digital editions rather than paid print formats. |
| Mattering Press | **The Ethnographic Case**, second edition, had CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and a canonical PDF returning HTTP 206/PDF bytes. | First/second editions are distinct records. Preserve noncommercial/share-alike terms for content reuse; this proposal is metadata discovery and outbound reading. |
| mediastudies.press | Selected second-edition record declared CC0 and supplied a canonical PDF returning HTTP 206/PDF bytes. | A same-title older edition had a different DOI/license. Do not merge by title or copy rights across editions. |
| punctum books | **Analogical City** had CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and a canonical publisher PDF returning HTTP 206/PDF bytes. | Returned location lists also contain retail and unreviewed third-party hosts. Only approved official/authorized locations can become reading links. |

File-access samples were 4 KiB, bounded to avoid bulk downloads. No complete books
or audio files are committed. Source API responses were examined locally; the
committed evidence retains only small metadata samples and request summaries.
Browser-verification pages and failed requests were not treated as usable content.

## Query behavior and operating constraints

All six retrieval families—GDL, MediaWiki, LoC JSON, Internet Archive search,
LibriVox and Thoth—were probed with a nonsense term. Empty results were observed;
LibriVox expresses this as HTTP 404 with an audiobook-not-found JSON message.
An adapter must distinguish that documented response shape from an outage.
Representative second-page requests were also checked; retain each provider's
paging and scope. These checks are evidence, not implemented app behavior.

Thoth publisher filters and active book types constrain results, but results are
not guaranteed to be ordered by reader relevance. They can match descriptions.
Wikisource needs whole-work/section handling. GDL needs token/phrase relevance
checks. These observations are particularly relevant to the earlier irrelevant
free-search results: a working API alone does not finish search quality.

No paid fallback is proposed. All tested search requests worked anonymously.
Respect current provider limits and use bounded requests, cancellation, backoff
and truthful unavailable states. No numeric unlimited allowance is inferred where
documentation does not publish one. Wikimedia calls should be serial with a
descriptive User-Agent and maxlag for research; Internet Archive also requests
identification of automated clients. LibriVox documents a maximum page size of
500 and pacing for bulk work. We requested only three catalog records at a time,
except GDL's fixed 20-record search page.

## Coverage and the next decision

G01 covers children, books, scholarly books/textbooks and audio. This first batch
demonstrates each broad area but is weighted toward scholarly publishers; it is
not ten sources per category. Hindi, Tamil and India-related historical material

# Books, children's reading and audiobooks: discovery recipes

Planning research, 2026-11-05. Covers C01, C02, C04 and C05 in the
[expansion plan](../EXPANSION_PLAN.md); published research articles C03 have a
separate recipe. Use the [qualification record](../SOURCE_REVIEW_TEMPLATE.md)
for every origin. Links below were inspected as documentation or directory leads;
this work does not establish a new working connector or enable a source.

The discovery chain is **directory/network → independently maintained catalog →
permitted retrieval route → matching item → evidenced free destination**. A
directory, an aggregator and the same underlying publisher are not three origins.
Reach 100 through additional useful catalogs, not additional mirrors, languages,
formats, narrators or books within a catalog.

## C01. Children's books and early literacy

**Best starting points.** [IBBY national sections](https://www.ibby.org/ibby-worldwide/ibby-sections)
provide country-level publishing/literacy networks, including India and the US.
Follow sections to publishers and literacy organizations with digital collections.
For India, [Parag's publisher and bookstore directory](https://www.paragreads.in/parag-reads/childrens-publishers-and-bookstores/)
is a concrete seed list; bookstores and commercial catalogs remain leads rather
than eligible sources. [Book Dash's partner network](https://bookdash.org/partners/)
links literacy organizations and content collaborators, including African
Storybook and Pratham Books. Distinguish content producers from organizations
that only distribute another publisher's books.

**Search process.** Create country × language × publisher-type cells: national
literacy NGOs, independent publishers, educational foundations and public bodies.
Start with English/Hindi/Tamil, then investigate other Indian scripts and
underrepresented African/Asian languages. For each network lead, search:

```text
site:{publisher-domain} ("free stories" OR "digital library" OR "open licence")
"{language}" "children's books" ("Creative Commons" OR "open access")
"{publisher name}" (metadata OR API OR catalog OR download)
"हिन्दी बाल कहानियाँ" "मुक्त" / "தமிழ் சிறுவர் கதைகள்" "இலவசம்"
```

Repeat the native-language pattern with locally appropriate vocabulary; search
terms are discovery prompts, not evidence that results are lawful or free. Follow
actual book credits back to publishers and translators. Expand in batches of 25
origins across new country/language cells; use the measured pass rate to replenish
the pool toward 100 qualified origins. A national section is not automatically a
publisher and a translation of the same catalog does not add an origin.

**Retrieval to investigate.** Prefer attributed coverage in an approved catalog,
an official export, or a supported publisher interface. An open-source website
codebase does not grant API access or metadata reuse. Free reader registration is
acceptable when disclosed; an advertised offer and verified post-login access are
separate observations. Recheck the existing StoryWeaver gate before expanding it.

**Category tests.** Find known titles in their original script; resolve the
specific translation, preserve writer/illustrator/translator credits and original
story relations, verify every page is accessible, and retain publisher levels
without inventing child ages. Test a wordless book, translated story and free-login
book where present. Do not turn a sample page into a complete reading action.

**First ten leads:** four India-origin publishers/NGOs from Parag and Pratham
connections, four publishers from other IBBY sections, and two independent
catalogs identified through Book Dash collaborators. Deduplicate shared catalogs;
deep-review one reusable-feed candidate and one multilingual candidate first.

## C02. General books and ebooks

**Best starting points.** [Project Gutenberg's official catalog documentation](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/offline_catalogs.html)
identifies machine-readable catalogs, OPDS and affiliate/mirror links. Use the
catalog as a retrieval model; mirrors are duplicate hosting. National libraries,
state digital libraries, regional literary organizations and university special
collections supply additional independent origins. The [Library of Congress
JSON/YAML interface](https://www.loc.gov/apis/json-and-yaml/) is a US starting
point for digitized collection records; its scope is not the entire library catalog.
DPLA's [developer documentation](https://pro.dp.la/developers/api-codex) is a
US aggregator lead requiring a fresh documentation/access check before selection.

**India route.** Start with state-library and language-academy institution lists,
then inspect the official digital catalogs. [Project Madurai](https://www.projectmadurai.org/)
is a concrete Tamil literature lead with a linked works list and text-format
information. Its reading/distribution statements do not by themselves establish
permission for the app's proposed metadata harvest. Investigate Hindi and other
regional literary catalogs through their actual operators rather than copying
anonymous “free PDF” lists.

**Search process.** Search `"{country/state}" "digital library" "literature"`,
`site:{institution-domain} ("digitized books" OR "ebooks" OR "rare books")`,
then `"{catalog name}" (OPDS OR MARC OR RDF OR API OR metadata)`. For each
national/state network, follow its digitization partners to catalog owners.
Expand the pool by geography, language and literature type; count independently
maintained catalogs only after recording attribution and a searchable subset.
Compare holdings with existing Gutenberg coverage before prioritizing a connector.

**Retrieval to investigate.** Import official reusable metadata into a bounded
local search artifact, use permitted OPDS search when available, or verify an
aggregator's origin attribution. Gutenberg's documentation currently mentions
OPDS2 testing and planned retirement of its XML OPDS feed in 2027; recheck before
choosing a long-term interface. Search-engine site results are not a substitute
for an in-app catalog. Record OCR/full-text availability separately from metadata
search; a digitized scan may be readable without searchable OCR.

**Category tests.** Recover exact title/author/edition; distinguish similar titles,
multi-volume sets and translated editions; test complete book versus excerpt,
cover-only object and loan. Resolve ISBNs only where supplied. Preserve original
script and Unicode. Record territorial rights evidence independently of the
server's ability to fetch a page; US public-domain status is not worldwide proof.

**First ten leads:** four Indian regional/institutional catalogs, four national
or university catalogs across other countries, and two independent public-domain
publishers. Existing Gutenberg is a comparison baseline, not a newly found source.

## C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters

**Best starting points.** [DOAB metadata](https://doabooks.org/en/librarians/doab-metadata)
documents CC0 exports and OAI-PMH, including selective publisher/subject exports.
Use publisher identities to discover origins and verify their actual OA subsets.
[Open Textbook Library discovery](https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks/discovery)
documents MARC/CSV, JSON resources and change feeds. Follow textbook publisher and
institution links into university presses and open-education programs. These
catalogs expose different kinds of books; keep textbooks, monographs and chapters
distinct even when the same publisher supplies all three.

**India route.** Investigate [NCERT's textbook catalog](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php),
state textbook bodies, university presses and e-PG Pathshala-linked institutions.
Start with official institution lists, then find their publication catalogs and
terms. An NCERT/state-board website with downloadable books is a candidate, not
evidence of an available external search API. Treat school medium, syllabus and
academic year as scope fields, not merely title keywords.

**Search process.** Enumerate publisher-origin candidates from approved metadata
exports by discipline, language and geography; inspect batches of 25 distinct
publishers. Search `"{university press}" "open access books"`,
`"{subject}" "open textbook" "{country}"`, and
`site:{education-body-domain} (textbook OR publication) (catalog OR download)`.
Follow open-education network members into their own catalogs and compare against
DOAB/OTL holdings. To approach 100, add qualified publisher catalogs across
disciplines, not 100 series from one press. Record the fraction actually covered
by the aggregator; a few OA titles never imply a wholly free publisher catalog.

**Retrieval to investigate.** Prefer DOAB/OTL-origin mapping and official exports
before custom publisher connectors. OAI-PMH needs an import and local keyword
index; it is not a topic-search API. Per-book licenses and destinations remain
separate from the metadata feed license. Verify withdrawn records, corrected
editions and bounded refresh costs without provisioning a hosted database.

**Category tests.** Find a known chapter and its parent book; preserve chapter DOI
versus book DOI/ISBN; check edition and syllabus year; distinguish instructor-only
solutions from the free student text. Include a broad topic such as mathematics
and specific concepts to test relevance rather than accepting every education
record. Sample multilingual titles and withdrawn/changed links where available.

**First ten leads:** four Indian educational publishers/institutions, four new
publishers represented in DOAB/OTL, and two independently maintained catalogs from
underrepresented regions. Deep-review a publisher represented by an export and
an India school-text catalog to compare integration and refresh effort.

## C05. Audiobooks and recorded books

**Best starting points.** [LibriVox API documentation](https://librivox.org/api/info)
describes ID, title, author and genre retrieval, JSON/XML responses and offset
paging. It presently caps `limit` at 500 and asks clients to space bulk requests;
recheck current policies before implementation. Use national-library audio
collections and independently maintained public-domain recording projects for
additional catalogs. [DAISY member organizations](https://daisy.org/about-us/membership/full-members/)
provide accessible-reading leads, with eligibility evaluated individually.

**US and India route.** The [NLS BARD documentation](https://www.loc.gov/apis/additional-apis/nlsbard-api/)
is an important counterexample: public metadata search exists, but full-item use
requires reader eligibility. Keep this outside the general free-reading count.
Investigate regional-language volunteer recording catalogs and public cultural
institutions in India. [Sugamya Pustakalaya](https://sugamyapustakalaya.org.in/)
is a discovery lead whose access conditions and supported retrieval still require
review; do not treat accessibility-service registration as ordinary free signup.

**Search process.** Search `"{language}" "public domain audiobooks"`,
`"{institution}" ("talking books" OR audiobooks) (catalog OR API OR RSS)`,
and native-script equivalents for recorded stories/books. Follow a catalog's
producer credits to independently maintained origins. Expand by language/country
and producer type; distinguish library catalogs, volunteer recording projects and
publishers. A LibriVox narrator, recording version or mirror is not a new origin.
Expect a lower qualification rate and document scarcity if 100 independent,
freely accessible catalogs cannot be established.

**Retrieval to investigate.** Use native catalog APIs, approved aggregator
metadata, or complete reusable feeds compiled locally. A podcast feed containing
recent episodes may cover only a short window, not a book archive. Preserve
recording ID, work relation, narrator, language, abridgement, chapter order and
duration. Link the original player or permitted file; do not rehost audio.

**Category tests.** Recover a known title/author; distinguish human readings,
synthetic narration and dramatization; verify the first, middle and final sections
of a purported complete recording. Check playable media versus trailers, expired
links and subscriptions. Test accented/native-script names, repeated recordings
of one work and a free-login destination where genuinely available.

**First ten leads:** four India-language recording/catalog operators, four
independent international audio origins and two library/cultural audio catalogs.
If eligible candidates are scarce, record deferred leads explicitly; do not fill
the batch with paid trials, disability-entitled collections or podcast episodes.

## Evidence boundaries and next handoff

Documentation opens succeeded for IBBY, Parag, Book Dash, Gutenberg, OTL, DOAB,
Project Madurai, LibriVox, DAISY and NLS during this planning review. The research
tool returned HTTP 402 for StoryWeaver's open-content page, 502 for NCERT's
textbook page and 403 for DPLA's API page. Sugamya redirected to its current domain
but exposed no readable content to the tool. These observations establish neither
payment requirements nor source-wide outages. No credentials, source accounts,
outreach, bulk harvests or live query qualification probes were performed.

Next deliverables: up to 40 deduplicated leads across these four categories,
eight deep reviews where suitable candidates exist, and a ranked integration
recommendation with actual pass rate, marginal coverage and operating effort.
Keep the parent plan's qualified/enabled distinction and existing access-expiry
rules throughout; this document does not refresh old reading evidence.

# Industry and job knowledge: twenty discovery tracks

Planning research, 2026-11-05. Companion to the [expansion plan](../EXPANSION_PLAN.md)
and [source review template](../SOURCE_REVIEW_TEMPLATE.md). The links below are
discovery entry points, not a list of qualified or enabled integrations.

## Group and tagging model

Expose **Industry and job knowledge** as a recognizable discovery group. Implement
its twenty sectors as cross-cutting tags, alongside occupation, task, jurisdiction
and the existing content categories. A pump-maintenance handbook can be tagged
water services, agriculture and facilities while retaining one item identity.
It remains a technical manual or learning resource; industry is not its format.

Use `industryIds`, source-supplied occupation codes/titles, `taskTerms`, content
kind, language, jurisdiction, publication/version date and equipment/process
context. Keep locally supplied occupation labels; do not automatically equate
different countries' qualifications. The [O*NET database](https://www.onetcenter.org/database.html)
and its [documented API](https://services.onetcenter.org/reference/start/overview)
can supply US role/task vocabulary. India's [National Classification of
Occupations](https://www.dge.gov.in/national_classification_of_occupations) supplies
another classification. Neither is a universal collection of practical manuals.

An eventual goal of 100 qualified origins **per industry tag** is a separate
coverage measure. It does not add 2,000 unique providers to the twenty content
categories' totals. Count each origin once globally, then report evidenced
industry/category memberships and searchable scope. Repeating one qualification
registry across twenty sectors is still one registry connector.

## Shared starting points

- **International:** [ILO sectors](https://www.ilo.org/topics-and-sectors/industries-and-sectors)
  links sector programs and guidance. Use its sector/country networks to find
  additional publishers. [FAO publications](https://www.fao.org/publications/en)
  links its knowledge repository; [WHO publications](https://www.who.int/publications)
  supplies health-related guidance; [IMO's Maritime Knowledge Centre](https://www.imo.org/en/knowledgecentre/pages/default.aspx)
  is a maritime discovery lead. Admission is per free item, not organization.
- **USA:** follow regulator publication catalogs, the [USDA land-grant institution
  directory](https://www.nifa.usda.gov/land-grant-colleges-and-universities-partner-website-directory)
  and [NIST MEP centers](https://www.nist.gov/mep/centers) into independently
  maintained extension/training catalogs. A center offering paid consulting can
  still publish free material; its whole service catalog is not free content.
- **India:** [NQR](https://www.nqr.gov.in/) exposes sectors, awarding bodies and
  job-role qualifications, and announces migration to [Kaushalverse](https://kaushalverse.ncvet.gov.in/homepage/repository).
  Check both during discovery and preserve original qualification IDs/version.
  [Bharat Skills](https://bharatskills.gov.in/) offers trade learning resources;
  [NSDC occupational standards and model curricula](https://nsdcindia.org/national-occupational-standards-and-model-curriculum)
  leads to sector councils and qualification packs. Their website search does
  not establish a reusable API or permission to reproduce metadata.

In the matrix, **catalog probe** means investigate a documented API, permitted
metadata export or bounded reusable index. It does not mean scrape whichever
internal endpoint powers a website. Searches are discovery recipes to run against
official sites, then repeat for other countries, languages and institutions.

every qualification has a publicly reusable handbook.

## Repeatable search and qualification process

Search the combination **industry × occupation × task × jurisdiction × content
kind**. Begin with a worker question such as “Hindi guide for a warehouse picker
handling cold-chain products.” Expand occupation synonyms using source-supplied
labels, task vocabularies and English/native-script variants. Keep transliteration
as a search aid; it does not establish content language.

For every industry, follow three independent discovery routes:

1. **Authority route:** sector regulator → publications/guidelines → state/local
   counterparts → independently maintained catalogs. Check applicability and
   version. Twenty departments publishing through one catalog are not twenty
   automatically qualified origins.
2. **Training route:** qualification register → awarding body/sector council →
   public handbook/curriculum catalog → institution publishers. Qualification
   descriptions alone establish skills or curriculum, not full training content.
3. **Practice route:** extension/technical-center network → institutional resource
   collections → official manufacturer/project manuals where freely accessible.
   Publisher member lists are candidate generators; membership proves no API.

Try exact strings such as `"{role}" "participant handbook"`,
`site:{official-domain} "{task}" (manual OR guide OR curriculum)` and native-script
equivalents. Then search the selected provider for `API`, `metadata`, `export`,
`repository`, `license` and `reuse`. External search-engine matches help find
providers; they do not become app catalog records by themselves.

Use a documented live/aggregator interface where available, otherwise a permitted
metadata import searched locally. A small static registry and bounded catalog
artifacts fit the existing no-new-datastore approach. Shared transport/parsers can
serve several sources, but permissions and field mapping remain source-specific.
Record metadata reuse separately from the right to read a publicly downloadable
manual; public availability alone does not authorize bulk reproduction.

The initial queue is five leads per industry, ideally two India, two US and one
international. These up-to-100 industry memberships overlap the master plan's
content-category survey. Deduplicate before selecting deep reviews and use the
master plan's aggregate cap. Prioritize agriculture, construction, manufacturing
and logistics in the first technical sample, while retaining all twenty tags in
the register. Subsequently use the common 10 → 25 → 50 → 100 ladder and observed
pass rate to refill each sector's candidate pool. Record sparse sectors honestly.

## Category-specific acceptance and evidence

Test a known handbook, a task query, a role synonym, one native-language query
where supported and an old/superseded edition. Retrieve the actual document and
its issuer/version, not a course-registration page. Sample whether a search for
an operator's task returns useful instructions rather than unrelated research
or executive policy reports. Preserve equipment/process model, qualification
code, units and jurisdiction when supplied. Do not synthesize missing metadata.

For safety-critical and regulated work, results should identify the authority,
audience and effective revision. Government/industry guidance, binding rules,
training texts and manufacturers' procedures remain distinguishable. An indexed
manual does not confer a job qualification, certification or approval.

Before enablement, prove item-level topic/title retrieval and stable resolution,
free full-item access, source permissions and refresh behavior under the shared
review template. Neither an O*NET occupational match nor an NQR qualification
match establishes that another provider has the requested manual. Identifier-only
resolvers support discovery but do not count toward searchable-origin targets.

## Documentation review limits

This review inspected primary web documentation/catalog pages, not production
API requests or a hundred sources per industry. O*NET explicitly documents an
API and downloadable data; reuse that as vocabulary evidence only until the
chosen integration is tested. The NQR migration notice was observed directly.
FDA/FAA/OSHA/NIST, ROSA P, FAO/WHO/IMO and Bharat Skills pages were readable.
India's ICAR, MSME, FSSAI, NHM and CERT-In discovery links also appeared in official
search results; catalog/permissions checks remain necessary.

NSDC's sector-council page and the FDIC page returned 403 in this research tool;
EPA NEPIS exposed no readable text. OSTI/MSHA/MARAD deep links were inaccessible,
and the older Forest Service Treesearch URL redirected to its research homepage.
These are unresolved research observations, not claims of service downtime.
Use official directory/root navigation to find current routes; do not turn a
browser restriction into an invented endpoint or relax the source admission gate.

# Language, culture and educational media discovery

Research playbook, 2026-11-05. Covers C14, C15, C16, C17 and C20 under the
[expansion plan](../EXPANSION_PLAN.md). Links establish discovery routes and
documented capabilities, not qualified or enabled sources. No endpoint probes,
account creation or paid services were used. Apply the
[source-review template](../SOURCE_REVIEW_TEMPLATE.md) to each proposed origin.

## C14 — Language learning and adult literacy

**Where to start.** The [Open Language Archives Community](https://www.language-archives.org/)
provides a language-resource discovery network; its
[FAQ](https://www.language-archives.org/documents/faq/) describes participating
archives and OAI metadata exchange. Filter for instructional materials: a
linguistic recording or restricted research corpus is not automatically a usable
language lesson. For US adult literacy, the
[LINCS resource collection](https://lincs.ed.gov/resource-collection) identifies
instructional producers and state/local program resources. In India,
[Bharatavani](https://www.bharatavani.in/home/dictionaries) identifies dictionaries,
glossaries, languages and contributing institutions; follow those producers to
their lesson, primer and literacy catalogs. Also investigate state literacy
missions and university language departments through official institution sites.

**Repeatable searches.** Run `"{language}" "adult literacy" "resources"`,
`"{institution}" (primer OR lessons OR metadata OR OAI-PMH)` and native-script
variants such as `"தமிழ்" "கற்றல்" "பாடங்கள்"` and
`"हिन्दी" "साक्षरता" "पुस्तिका"`. Search the official institution domain after
finding an organization; record target language separately from teaching language.

**Toward 100.** Sample ten candidates: four Indian language/education producers,
two US adult-literacy organizations and four from language archives or other
countries. Expand by language family, literacy audience and institutional
producer in batches of 25. Reuse one producer across applicable categories but
count its language tabs only once. A large number of language collections does
not establish 100 independent instructional origins.

**Retrieval and tests.** Investigate attributed aggregator records and permitted
OAI/catalog imports. LINCS/Bharatavani website search alone does not establish a
reusable external API. Test an exact primer, a target-language topic, native
script, transliteration, an adult-versus-child distinction and the complete
lesson/audio destination. Preserve proficiency labels when supplied; do not infer
them from word count. Corpus access restrictions and missing machine interfaces
are likely reasons to defer candidates. Deep-review two distinct producers first.

## C15 — Historical documents, manuscripts and archives

**Where to start.** Use [Archives Portal Europe's institution directory](https://www.archivesportaleurope.net/find-an-institution/)
to branch by country and holding institution. Its current page directs researchers
to institution search while directory work continues. In the US,
[NARA's Catalog API documentation](https://www.archives.gov/research/catalog/help/api)
describes keyword/search-result and individual-record JSON retrieval. Extend
discovery through state archives, university special collections and municipal
archive directories. In India, the National Archives'
[Abhilekh Patal description](https://nationalarchives.nic.in/en/online-portal-abhilekh-patal)
is the national starting point; follow state archives, regional record centers
and university manuscript collections separately.

**Repeatable searches.** Use `"{country/state}" "archives" "digital collections"`,
`site:{archive-domain} (EAD OR OAI-PMH OR API OR "metadata download")`, and
`"{place}" "{date range}" "{document type}"`. Search historic and current place
names. For India add `"{state}" "अभिलेखागार"` and the local-script equivalent;
for the US include county/city archives after state-level discovery.

**Toward 100.** Start with four Indian holding institutions, two US federal/state
origins and four non-US international archives. Replenish from institutional
directories and regional archival networks. Record centers under one maintained
catalog are collections unless independent catalog stewardship is demonstrated.
Neither a directory's institution total nor a count of archival finding aids is
the enabled-source total.

**Retrieval and tests.** Prefer supported archival search or licensed EAD/OAI
exports with origin attribution. NARA documents a machine route; current key,
terms and limits still require review. Abhilekh Patal's external integration route
is unverified here. A finding aid may describe an undigitized box: require an
actual digitized object for usable online access. Test collection → series → item
hierarchy, reference code, date range, historical place aliases and a multipage
object. A IIIF manifest can describe/display a known object; separately prove
catalog discovery. Flag missing OCR rather than promising handwritten full-text
search. Deep-review one supported catalog and one Indian-origin candidate first.

## C16 — Museums, art and cultural heritage

**Where to start.** [Europeana's API overview](https://www.europeana.eu/en/apis)
describes search, record and harvesting routes with contributing institutions.
Use provider attribution to discover museums across countries, then check the
institution's own open-collection policy. In India,
[Museums of India's digitization initiative](https://museumsofindia.gov.in/repository/page/digitization_initiative)
links participating museums, with JATAN as the collection-management context.
This is a useful network of leads; it does not establish a public integration API.
For the US investigate museum open-access programs and official collection
developer pages, including Smithsonian as a lead requiring renewed documentation.

**Repeatable searches.** Run `"{country}" "museum" "open access collections"`,
`site:{museum-domain} (API OR IIIF OR "collection data" OR "metadata download")`
and `"{Indian state}" "museum" "digital collection"`. Follow departmental
collection links to confirm who maintains the catalog before assigning an origin.

**Toward 100.** First ten: four Indian museums, two US institutions and four
international museums identified through aggregators. Expand by institution,
country and collection discipline: visual art, archaeology, textiles, craft,
natural history and technology. Different departments, exhibitions and objects
under one catalog do not become additional sources. Measure whether an added
institution contributes new languages or material rather than duplicate records.

**Retrieval and tests.** Prefer attributed aggregate search or official catalog
APIs/exports. Keep object metadata rights, image rights and physical-object
ownership separate. Verify an object identifier, creator/culture where supplied,
date uncertainty, place, institution and viewable media. Test a known object,
material/technique query, multilingual title and duplicate depiction. A tiny
thumbnail or metadata-only entry does not prove access to usable educational
media; declare the available representation. Require item-level permission and
attribution, including any restriction notices. Deep-review one aggregator-backed
origin and one direct-origin route before proposing a shared museum connector.

## C17 — Newspapers, magazines and public-interest articles

**Where to start.** Separate historic newspaper repositories from current
publishers. The [Library of Congress Chronicling America API page](https://www.loc.gov/apis/additional-apis/chronicling-america-api/)
states that the collection moved exclusively to the loc.gov API beginning in
2025; do not reuse old `chroniclingamerica.loc.gov` integration recipes.
Europeana and national libraries provide additional historical leads. For current
US/local journalism, [INN's Find Your News directory](https://findyournews.org/)
leads to publishers by place and topic. India's
[Press Registrar title directory](https://prgi.gov.in/en/test/registred-titles)
supports discovery by publication place, state and language. Registration proves
neither free article access nor permission to reuse metadata.

**Repeatable searches.** Use `"{state/language}" "digitized newspapers"`,
`"{city}" "nonprofit newsroom"`, and
`site:{publisher-domain} (RSS OR API OR syndication OR "reuse policy")`.
For India combine local-script publication names with archive/date terms. Follow
each title to the actual publisher; exclude reseller and subscription-preview
pages from free-source qualification.

**Toward 100.** First ten: two Indian historical collections, two Indian current
publishers, two US archival/news origins and four other-country origins. Expand
by language, city/state, publication period and publisher network. Several titles
owned by the same maintained publisher catalog remain one origin. A syndication
copy does not automatically constitute new reporting coverage.

**Retrieval and tests.** Investigate supported archive APIs or permitted publisher
feeds/exports. [WordPress documents searchable post retrieval](https://developer.wordpress.org/rest-api/reference/posts/),
but a publisher's deployed endpoint and external-use terms still need validation.
RSS may contain only recent headlines; declare that window or find a supported
back-catalog route. Test issue/date/page identity separately from article identity,
OCR versus title matches, corrections, paywall/preview exclusions and original
publisher attribution. Test an older article beyond the first feed page before
claiming historical search. Deep-review one archive and one current publisher;
mixed paywalls and unclear reuse policies are expected qualification losses.

## C20 — Educational podcasts, lectures and documentaries

**Where to start.** Begin with universities, public educational broadcasters and
institutional media producers, following their series/catalog links. In India,
[NPTEL's course catalog](https://nptel.ac.in/courses) provides instructor/course
and institutional discovery leads; investigate official educational broadcaster
and university series alongside it. For international and US material, inspect
university lecture catalogs and public-media learning collections. The
[Internet Archive developer portal](https://archive.org/developers/) documents
metadata tools for archive-hosted media; [Wikimedia Commons API guidance](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:API)
supports another metadata route, with license and exclusion markers to review.

**Repeatable searches.** Run `"{university/broadcaster}" "public lectures"`,
`"{subject}" "educational podcast" "RSS"`, and
`site:{official-domain} ("media catalog" OR API OR "video lectures" OR feed)`.
For India include Hindi/Tamil topic terms and the producer's official language
channel. A commercial streaming-platform listing is only a discovery clue.

**Toward 100.** First ten: four Indian educational producers, two US producers
and four elsewhere. Expand by discipline, teaching language and institutional
network; count the producing catalog once across its video channel, podcast feed
and mirror. Series, playlists and episodes are not independent source origins.
Full documentaries with suitable access and reusable discovery may be scarcer
than lectures; publish that gap rather than filling it with trailers.

**Retrieval and tests.** Prefer documented catalogs, attributed archive records
or permitted RSS/Atom imports. NPTEL's visible catalog does not establish an
external API in this review. Preserve episode/lecture ID, series/course relation,
producer, language, date, duration and canonical playback URL. Test a complete
recording, removed media, country restriction, premium-only episode and a caption
or transcript where available. Metadata search must not be described as searching
every spoken word. Hosting on an archive or public platform does not establish
lawful free access for every upload. Deep-review one feed-based producer and one
catalog-based producer before selecting a reusable media connector.

## Evidence limits and research handoff

This pass reviewed official documentation and directory pages on 2026-11-05.
NARA, Archives Portal Europe, National Archives of India, Museums of India,
Bharatavani, Europeana, PRGI, INN/Find Your News, loc.gov, NPTEL, Internet Archive,
Commons and WordPress pages were retrievable. OLAC FAQ and LINCS direct opens
returned 403 despite official search-index descriptions; treat those details as
leads pending direct recheck. Smithsonian `openaccess/devtools` and
`openaccess/faq` opens returned 404 despite indexed results; locate their current
official documentation before qualification. These observations do not establish
service-wide failure or full-item availability.

The first research batch is 50 category memberships, deduplicated globally, with
up to ten deep reviews across these five categories. Use the parent plan's
10 → 25 → 50 → 100 ladder, pass-rate estimates and required access/queryability
gates. Store only permitted metadata/evidence in the existing Git research
register; no new hosted data store is needed for this planning work.

# Learning and technical knowledge: discovery playbook

Planning research, 2026-11-05. Covers C09–C13 in the
[expansion plan](../EXPANSION_PLAN.md). Apply its source-count, free-access and
queryability gates using the [review record](../SOURCE_REVIEW_TEMPLATE.md).
The [industry playbook](INDUSTRIES.md) supplies occupation/sector tags; the
categories here describe the learning material. A welding manual can be a C13
guide with manufacturing and construction tags, without becoming three origins.

The linked official pages were reviewed as discovery/documentation evidence.
No API qualification, source signup, production integration or 100-source census
was performed. Directories identify publishers; they do not certify their
catalogs. API documentation does not establish our permission, quota suitability
or actual item access. Bounded permitted metadata imports remain available under
the current no-new-hosted-datastore design.

## C09 — School lessons, curricula and examination resources

**Start with curriculum owners, then follow their resource producers.**
[OER Commons collections](https://help.oercommons.org/support/solutions/articles/42000046866-browse-collections)
provide discovery by subject, educational level, material type and language.
For the US, follow state education departments and their linked district/OER
initiatives to the original publishers. Globally, repeat the process through
national education ministries and teacher-training institutions; a publisher
represented in several hubs remains one origin.

In India, start with [DIKSHA's discovery documentation](https://diksha.gov.in/help/getting-started/explore-diksha/),
which describes anonymous exploration and language/location filtering. Follow
the named content organizations to SCERTs, state boards and teacher-training
institutions. [NCERT's textbook portal](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) is a
lead for official textbook identities, alongside state textbook bodies and
examination-board archives. Treat textbooks shared with C04 as overlapping
category membership, not extra origins. The NCERT page returned 502 in this
review; its current retrieval route remains unverified.

**Search recipe:** choose a board/ministry, grade band, subject and language;
search its official domain for `curriculum`, `teacher guide`, `lesson`, `question
paper`, and the equivalent local-language terms. Example:
`site:{board-domain} "Class 8" "science" "2025"`; then
`"{publisher}" (metadata OR API OR export OR repository)`.
Expand in batches across states, curriculum authorities and independent
nonprofit producers rather than counting grade/subject folders as sources.

**Retrieval and tests:** investigate official catalogs, permitted exports or
attributed aggregator coverage. A DIKSHA browser endpoint is not automatically
a supported third-party API. Require item-level board, grade, medium, subject,
curriculum year and canonical resource identity where supplied. Test one lesson
in native script, a retired syllabus, a paper and its answer key, and a topic
shared across different grades. Reject unrelated or obsolete material masquerading
as the current curriculum. Preserve free enrollment versus paid examination rules.

## C10 — Courses, lecture notes and teaching materials

**Start with teaching institutions, not course-count leaderboards.** The
[Open Education Global member directory](https://www.oeglobal.org/about-us/members-list/)
is a repeatable route to international institutional leads, including community
colleges and regional open-education networks. Investigate each member's own
open course catalog, repository and public lecture-note collections. Membership
alone does not mean that it publishes eligible material. Use institutional
OpenCourseWare catalogs, including [MIT OCW](https://ocw.mit.edu/search/), as
examples of course organization; this review extracted only a shell from MIT's
search page, so it establishes no machine-search route.

For India, [SWAYAM's official overview](https://swayam.gov.in/about) identifies
national coordinators including NPTEL, UGC, CEC, NCERT, NIOS and IGNOU. Follow
coordinator → participating institution → official course/lesson catalog.
Record the producer institution and distribution platform separately. SWAYAM
describes free course learning and paid certification exams; the destination's
actual learning-access conditions still need review.

**Search recipe:** `site:{institution-domain} ("open courseware" OR "lecture
notes" OR "course materials") "{subject}"`, followed by semester/course-code
queries. Sample humanities and social sciences as well as engineering; expand
through country, language and discipline. University departments within one
shared catalog are not independently counted origins by default.

**Retrieval and tests:** seek supported course feeds, reusable metadata exports
or repository harvesting. Preserve institution, course code, semester/version,
lesson order and language. Search must return a course or a named lesson that
can actually be opened; a certificate-registration page is insufficient. Probe
an archived course, a current course, a free-account course, accessible notes and
caption/transcript availability. Check whether enrollment dates affect access.
Never infer that downloading one lecture grants rights to redistribute the course.

## C11 — Encyclopedias, dictionaries and reference works

**Find reference publishers by discipline and language.** Start with scholarly
and national-library reference guides, then follow their primary publishers.
For wiki-based works, [MediaWiki's search documentation](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Search)
describes title/content queries and namespace selection. Identify the actual
reference work and operator before selecting an endpoint; wiki software is a
connector family, not an assurance that every deployment permits external use.

In India, [Bharatavani's dictionary collection](https://www.bharatavani.in/home/dictionaries)
is a lead to multilingual dictionaries, glossaries and their publishers. Its
catalog describes both searchable and PDF-based resources. Follow credited
language academies, universities and terminology bodies, and investigate local
reference resources in Hindi, Tamil and additional scripts. Elsewhere, use the
same language-academy/university approach rather than filling the register with
English-language general encyclopedias.

**Search recipe:** `"{discipline}" (encyclopedia OR glossary OR dictionary)
"{language}"` and native terms such as `शब्दकोश` or `அகராதி`; validate official
ownership, then search for API/export/licensing documentation. Expand across
disciplinary reference publishers and separately maintained works. Language
views, namespaces, dictionary editions and mirrors do not create extra origins.

**Retrieval and tests:** distinguish entry-level search from book-title search.
A scanned dictionary searchable only by its title cannot answer a headword
query. Test a homonym, inflected form, native-script spelling, transliteration,
cross-reference and missing term. Preserve headword, sense/entry ID, language,
edition or revision and source authority. Do not label a partial OCR hit as an
exact definition. Public reading and permission to reuse definition text are
separate decisions; show minimal permitted metadata and link to the entry.

## C12 — Technical documentation and software manuals

**Start from official projects and vendors, then locate versioned documentation.**
The [CNCF project directory](https://www.cncf.io/projects/) is one concrete
project-discovery network. Expand through other software foundations, language
communities, public research-software organizations and official hardware/tool
manufacturers. Include India-based public technology projects and institute
software catalogs by searching official organization domains; do not classify
every tool used in India as an India-origin source.

[Read the Docs documents a project/version search API](https://docs.readthedocs.com/platform/stable/server-side-search/api.html).
Its [API v3 documentation](https://docs.readthedocs.com/platform/stable/api/v3.html)
also describes authentication and request limits, including five unauthenticated
requests per minute at review time. This is a promising connector family, with
a capacity and permissions question to resolve before enabling it. An alternative
is an explicitly licensed documentation source/export compiled into a bounded
metadata index. Public repository visibility alone is not a license.

**Search recipe:** directory → official project website → documentation/repository
→ supported search/export/version information. Use `"{project}" "documentation"
"{version}"`, then `site:{docs-domain} "{task or symbol}"`. Expand across
independently maintained project catalogs and subject families. Retain parent
organization identity to avoid counting every repository, release, locale or
hosted mirror as an independent source.

**Retrieval and tests:** identify project, stable version, page/section, language
and canonical link. Test a symbol renamed between releases, a deprecated command,
two projects using the same term, a version-pinned page and a section anchor.
Search snippets must not be mistaken for complete procedural instructions.
Ensure redirects do not silently change a saved version. Exclude paid manuals
and standards that expose only a title or purchase page. This workstream covers
technical documents; occupation/industry applicability belongs in the linked
industry tags.

## C13 — Practical, vocational and agricultural guides

**Use extension and training networks as the expansion engine.** The
[UNEVOC network directory](https://connect.unevoc.unesco.org/home/Explore%2Bthe%2BUNEVOC%2BNetwork)
provides country/region/institution leads for vocational education. Follow each
center to public course-material and practical-guide publishers. For the US,
[NIFA's land-grant institution directory](https://www.nifa.usda.gov/land-grant-colleges-and-universities-partner-website-directory)
provides a systematic route to university extension publication catalogs; county
offices republishing the same university guide do not increase origin counts.

In India, [Bharat Skills](https://bharatskills.gov.in/) describes a central
repository of curricula, course material, videos and question banks. Trace its
trade resources to DGT/NIMI and credited producers. The
[ICAR institution directory](https://www.icar.gov.in/en/institutions) supports
discovery by research division, followed by institutes, agricultural universities
and extension/KVK publication leads. Apply the industry playbook to agriculture,
construction, manufacturing and other sectors instead of inventing separate
categories for every job title.

**Search recipe:** choose occupation → concrete task → skill level → region;
query `site:{institution-domain} (manual OR handbook OR extension OR workbook)
"{task}"`, then publication-series and native-language variants. Expand across
training networks, independent extension publishers, countries and occupations;
do not count every trade PDF as a source.

**Retrieval and tests:** seek publication exports, allowed repository harvests
or attributed metadata feeds. Store occupation/industry tags, task, intended
audience, language, revision and geographic applicability. Test one task with
multiple regional recommendations, two editions of a manual, a multilingual
guide and a training course that requires payment. Verify the exact complete
guide and its publication date. A material's safety or legal currency must not
be inferred from government branding or a recent metadata refresh.

Create ten candidate records for each category, targeting four India origins,
two US origins and four other international origins. Where the pool is sparse,
record the gap and use another documented discovery route. Deep-review two per
category before extrapolating; the ten reviews should exercise distinct retrieval
methods rather than ten copies of one platform.

| Category | First two technical/access reviews |
| --- | --- |
| C09 | One Indian curriculum catalog and one independently maintained teacher-OER catalog |
| C10 | One coordinator-linked Indian course origin and one international university's reusable catalog |
| C11 | One supported entry-search wiki and one Indian dictionary/terminology catalog, explicitly testing search depth |
| C12 | One version-aware documentation API candidate and one licensed documentation-export candidate |
| C13 | One Indian training/extension catalog and one US or other-country practical-publication catalog |

Continue in batches of 25 candidates, adding underrepresented countries,
languages, disciplines and occupations until the 10 → 25 → 50 → 100 qualified
ladder is reached or a documented shortfall emerges. Report pass rate, overlap,
incremental useful coverage and maintainer effort per category. Site search alone
does not advance a source to qualified. No external outreach or source accounts
were created during this planning review.

Planning review: 2026-11-05. This playbook expands C08, C18 and C19 in the
[expansion plan](../EXPANSION_PLAN.md). It gives civic records, property and
geological maps explicit research tracks. Local discovery starts in **the USA
and India**. These are researched entry points and proposed qualification work;
no new source integrations or individual property records were collected here.

## Research matrix

Keep the **record type** column in the source register and progress report.
The P01–P09 tracks below subdivide existing categories; they do not create nine
additional 100-source quotas. A government's departments, datasets and map layers
are not automatically independent origins: apply the master counting rules.

| Track / record type | USA: where to find origins | India: where to find origins | Required query and result identity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **P01 Government, research and development reports — C08** | [GovInfo Developer Hub](https://www.govinfo.gov/developers), agency publication catalogs, state research bureaus, municipal annual reports; follow publishing agencies from catalog records | Ministry/department publication sections reached through the [National Portal](https://www.india.gov.in/); RBI, NITI Aayog, research councils and state economic-survey series as leads | Topic/title/year/issuing body → report ID, edition, publication date and full report. A press release announcing a report is not the report. |
| **P02 Laws, rules and gazettes — C18** | GovInfo, official federal regulations, state legislatures and local ordinance publishers linked from government websites | [India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/indiacode/home.jsp), Union/state gazettes, legislature sites and official rules collections | Act/rule number, title, section, jurisdiction and effective date → authoritative document/version. Distinguish tender announcement, award and expenditure. |

Separate owner field, assessment, tax bill, deed, record of rights and mutation. None alone becomes our independent certification of current legal title. |
| **P05 Building permits, zoning and planning — C18/C19** | Municipal building/planning departments, permit open-data catalogs, zoning GIS, adopted comprehensive plans and public planning decisions | Urban local bodies, development authorities, town/country planning departments and state municipal portals | Permit/application ID, address/parcel, zoning designation or area → document/feature plus application status, decision date and effective plan version. A proposal is distinct from an adopted plan or issued permit. |

Keep geology, mineral exploration, soil classification and probabilistic hazard distinct. |
