Distinguish present-day topography from historical sheets, satellite imagery and cadastral boundaries. |
| **P08 Census, statistics and time series — C19** | [Census developer geography guidance](https://www.census.gov/data/developers/geography.html), official statistical agencies and state/local statistical bureaus | OGD India, MoSPI, Census of India, RBI statistics and state statistical abstracts as source families | Topic/indicator + geography + period → dataset/table/series ID, unit, denominator, geography code and reference period. Housing-tenure statistics are aggregate information, not a register of individual owners. |
| **P09 Environmental and public infrastructure data — C19** | Federal/state environmental, water and transport agencies; public utilities' published datasets; local open-data catalogs | Pollution-control boards, water/public-works departments, transport authorities and state/city open-data catalogs | Facility/station/route/area + variable/time → public observation, inventory, permit or infrastructure dataset. Distinguish measured observations, modeled values and proposed infrastructure. |

## Find sources systematically, jurisdiction by jurisdiction

Build two jurisdiction trees before gathering hundreds of URLs. For the USA use
federal → state/territory → county/equivalent → municipality, recording tribal
government catalogs where appropriate. Start from [USAGov state links](https://www.usa.gov/state-governments)
and its local directory, then verify the actual agency responsible for the record.
Use official geography identifiers where supplied; the [Census API geography
documentation](https://www.census.gov/data/developers/geography.html) illustrates
why a county code without its state is ambiguous.

For India use Union → state/UT → district → subdistrict/tehsil → municipality or
village/panchayat. The [India district web directory](https://www.india.gov.in/directory/web-directory/districts)
and [Local Government Directory dataset](https://data.gov.in/catalog/local-government-directory-lgd)
are starting points. Follow official revenue, registration, planning, statistical
and geological offices from there. Record renamed/split districts and the vintage
of boundary codes; a village name alone is not a stable record identity.

For each of C08/C18/C19, expand an initial pool toward roughly 50–75 US and
50–75 India candidate origins, then replenish from observed pass rates. Sample
across geography, language, urban/rural context and government level. To approach
100 qualified sources, broaden jurisdictions and responsible agencies rather
than counting 100 datasets from one city as 100 sources. National aggregators
can cover several attributed origins, but membership and coverage require proof.

Research queries vary by record type:

```text
P01: site:{agency-domain} (publications OR reports) "{topic}" "{year}"
P02: site:{legislature-or-gazette-domain} "{act/rule title}" "{jurisdiction}"
P03: site:{city-domain} (minutes OR resolutions OR budget OR awards) "{year}"
P04: "{county/state}" (recorder OR assessor OR land records) (API OR open data)
P05: site:{planning-domain} (permits OR zoning OR master plan) (catalog OR GIS)
P06: "{state}" "geological survey" (map catalog OR GIS OR publications)
P07: site:{mapping-agency-domain} "{place/sheet}" (topographic OR land cover)
P08: site:{statistics-domain} "{indicator}" "{district/county}" (table OR API)
P09: site:{agency-domain} "{water/transport/environment theme}" (data OR services)
```

Use native-script/local terms for India, including भूलेख, खसरा, खतौनी, பட்டா and
சிட்டா where relevant. Keep the official terminology and script in results;
transliteration is a discovery aid, not authority to join two records. Search
engine hits identify candidates; they do not establish access or record contents.

## From a directory entry to something the app can query

Investigate these routes in order, and record the actual supported capabilities:

1. **Official document/dataset catalog API.** [GovInfo documents an API search
   service](https://www.govinfo.gov/features/search-service-overview) for content
   and metadata. The current [Data.gov Catalog API](https://resources.data.gov/catalog-api/)
   searches dataset metadata and identifies publisher organizations; it explicitly
   replaces the previous CKAN API. Use the current interface and key policy,
   not an old tutorial. An indexed dataset still needs a valid resource link.
2. **Approved exports and local metadata search.** Small DCAT/CSV/JSON/XML catalogs
   can become bounded, reviewed search artifacts without a hosted database. Prefer
   metadata and canonical outbound links; do not copy whole national parcel or
   imagery stores to make a prototype searchable.
3. **Native record or feature queries.** A source can qualify for property or
   spatial lookup through real address/parcel/document-ID/area queries even when
   it lacks general keyword search. This must return record metadata and a usable
   destination; an identifier-shaped redirect to an external search page is not
   retrieval. Record this as a separate capability from topic discovery.
4. **Geo services with explicit discovery.** [OGC WFS](https://www.ogc.org/standards/wfs/),
   [OGC API Features](https://www.ogc.org/standards/ogcapi-features/) and documented
   [ArcGIS layer queries](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/query-feature-service-layer/)
   are patterns to inspect for spatial/attribute filtering. Confirm the deployed
   service's capabilities, limits, IDs and terms; the platform brand is not proof.
   [WMS](https://www.ogc.org/standards/wms/)/WMTS primarily deliver rendered maps
   or tiles. A searchable layer catalog can support map discovery, but does not
   establish searchable parcel attributes or downloadable source features.

Track three separate capabilities: **find a dataset/map/document**, **query
records within it**, and **read/view/download the result**. A catalog hit for
property data cannot answer “which record covers this parcel?” unless the second
capability is present. Conversely a spatial result can be useful without hosting
a map renderer: a precise official map/document link is a valid initial action.

Maintain one selected live connector per request and bounded local searches.
Route by explicit country/jurisdiction, record type and supported query mode;
do not fan out to every county or district. The register records unsearched
coverage. A failed jurisdiction query does not establish absence of the record.

## Property and maps: two concrete pilot cases

**USA property:** NYC's official ACRIS page documents searchable property records
and document images for four boroughs, and also states bandwidth/automation
restrictions. Investigate the separately published [ACRIS Master dataset](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/City-Government/ACRIS-Real-Property-Master/bnx9-e6tj)
and its native data dictionary as a metadata route; prove document/parcel joins,
current terms and canonical image links before qualification. Do not extrapolate
its geographic coverage to all New York City or all US counties. This is one
illustrative local case, not a model every recorder must support.

**India property:** Tamil Nadu's official land e-services page lists rural
Patta/Chitta/FMB and urban TSLR resources and describes free FMS copies. It also
warns that automatic translation can change names in Tamil extracts. These facts
make it a strong discovery lead; they do not demonstrate an authorized external
API. Check supported metadata/record interfaces, the actual free access path,
survey/subdivision identifiers and allowed automation before enabling it. Service
or certification fees are distinct from freely viewing an informational record.

For both, preserve issuer, jurisdiction, record type and “as of” date. Assessment
roll ownership, recorded transaction parties, records of rights and registered
title serve different purposes. Return the official source's classification and
published redactions; do not silently infer current ownership from an older deed
or build unrelated personal profiles by joining records across authorities.

For maps, store native map/layer/sheet ID, source URL, geographic extent, coordinate
reference system, axis order, scale/resolution, legend, survey/observation date,
publication/update date and data lineage where provided. A geology map at regional
scale must not appear to be a precise parcel survey. Survey date and download
date are separate; historic maps remain historical even when newly digitized.

## First batch and acceptance tests

Allocate **six US and six India origins within the overall 60-origin deep-review
cap**, deduplicating any shared candidates. This is not an additional 12 reviews.
For each country select one reports/law route, one civic-budget route, one
property route, one permits/planning route, one geological/topographic route and
one statistics/environment route. Within a broad national catalog, inspect the
origin-specific attribution; include state/local cases rather than selecting
only national aggregators. NYC and Tamil Nadu are initial local case studies.

Before the next batch, complete the [source review template](../SOURCE_REVIEW_TEMPLATE.md)
and these track-specific checks using provider examples or public institutional
locations where possible:

- **Reports/law/civics:** retrieve a known document by title and number, separate
  amendments and editions, recover a dated meeting/decision and prove fiscal-year
  filtering. Confirm the canonical complete document rather than its announcement.
- **Property/planning:** test native parcel/address/document lookup in the correct
  jurisdiction; ambiguous address and nonexistent parcel; leading zeros; parcel
  splits/renumbering; mismatched assessment versus deed dates; permit status versus
  approved plan. Display unavailable/unknown when the requested join is unsupported.
- **Geology/maps:** retrieve a known sheet by ID and bounding box; test an extent
  crossing administrative boundaries; verify longitude/latitude order and CRS;
  distinguish map layer, legend and feature response. Check scale/date constraints,
  no-coverage responses and source-service limits without stress-testing the host.
- **Statistics/environment:** test geography code plus period, units, denominator,
  missing/suppressed values and boundary-vintage changes. Never convert a missing
  observation into zero or present an aggregate estimate as a household fact.
- **All tracks:** prove usable free access, paging/export bounds, permission,
  current source attribution and at least two representative sessions. Fixture-test
  failures and quotas. Free registration is acceptable; CAPTCHA, paid document
  access or restricted APIs may require deferral, never circumvention.

Report progress by country, government level, P-track and capability. For each
of C08/C18/C19 pursue the 10 → 25 → 50 → 100 qualified-origin ladder using measured
conversion and geographic gaps. Separately report origins enabled in the product;
one source's 5,000 layers does not replace the 100-origin goal.

## Evidence status and next verification

This was documentation research, not an API qualification run. Current official
Data.gov, GovInfo, USGS TNM, Census, USAGov, NYC and Tamil Nadu pages were readable;
their documentation supports the proposed discovery routes, not an availability
guarantee. Data.gov's current migration notice is especially important for future
connector selection. Keys, terms, quota settings and actual result samples still
need checking before implementation.

Direct opens of data.gov.in timed out, DILRMP's older state-link page and NGDRS
state links returned 502 in the research tool, NGMDB returned 403, and the older
Bhuvan WMS wiki URL returned 404 despite remaining in search results. Bhuvan's
homepage exposed only a loading shell; NGDR terms could not be opened. Official
search results identified GSI/NGDR and land-directory leads, but no machine-query
or free post-login behavior is certified. Record these gaps and recheck the
operator's current documentation; do not interpret the tool failures as national
service outages or a reason to invent an endpoint.

# Scholarly research discovery playbook

Planning research, 2026-11-05. Covers C03 published articles, C06 theses and
dissertations, and C07 preprints/working papers. Apply the counting and admission
rules in [the expansion plan](../EXPANSION_PLAN.md) and record each investigation
with [the source template](../SOURCE_REVIEW_TEMPLATE.md). These are documented
research routes; no new origin has been qualified or enabled by this review.

## C03 — Published research articles

**Start with publisher and repository discovery, then prove individual holdings.**
[OpenDOAR](https://opendoar.ac.uk/help/about) supplies institutional repository
leads. [SciELO](https://www.scielo.org/en/) supplies country, publisher and subject
entry points, particularly useful for Latin American and regional-language
coverage. DOAJ remains a directory lead; the current direct DOAJ connector
deferral is unchanged. Separate the publisher, journal collection, repository
copy and index that found it.

| Research track | Where to look and how to expand |
| --- | --- |
| International | Follow SciELO's publisher lists and country nodes; use OpenDOAR to identify university/research repositories; inspect disciplinary society publishers. Rotate medicine, engineering, agriculture, social sciences and humanities instead of taking the first 100 biomedical origins. |
| USA | Start with university repository catalogs and official learned-society publication lists. Separate institution-hosted open manuscripts from subscription publisher versions. Federal research agencies can also supply journal-article deposits; an agency bibliography alone is insufficient. |
| India | Use [INFLIBNET's initiatives](https://www.inflibnet.ac.in/activities/) and [university directory](https://web.inflibnet.ac.in/universitydirectory/index.php) to locate official institution sites. Follow their repository and society-publisher links, sampling central/state universities and research institutes. ONOS/N-LIST institutional entitlements are not evidence of anonymous public access. |

Repeatable discovery searches:

```text
site:{official-university-domain} (repository OR "open access") "{discipline}"
"{society name}" journals (metadata OR OAI-PMH OR API)
"{Indian institution}" (शोध OR ஆய்வு OR research) repository
```

Resolve organization names to stable identities before counting. The first
research batch is ten independent origins: four Indian, four broadly accessible
international and two additional regional-language origins. Deep-review one
publisher and one repository with the greatest apparent coverage gap. Expand in
25-origin batches across countries, disciplines and organization types toward
100 qualified origins; journal titles from one catalog do not become 100 origins.

**Retrieval strategy.** Test existing OpenAlex coverage first, using a known work
and its actual host attribution. Current [OpenAlex search documentation](https://help.openalex.org/api/searching/)
describes work text/keyword search and separate entity searches; an institution
name match does not establish that its repository holds the paper. Use the
documented filters and inspect individual locations. Preserve the existing free
allowance guard. A new publisher API or permitted OAI/export import is justified
when the index demonstrably misses useful holdings. An OJS website or a DOI
registration record alone does not prove reusable full-item discovery.

**Category-specific proof.** Use five known articles spanning recent/older years,
at least two subjects and relevant local-language content. Confirm topic relevance
with agriculture, manufacturing or another industry topic, not just exact titles.
Resolve DOI/native ID to the same article and test its free destination. Include
a hybrid-journal paywalled article, accepted manuscript versus published version,
retraction/correction and missing full-text location where present. Keep valid
versions distinct; a source-wide OA label cannot make every location free.

## C06 — Theses and dissertations

**Start from degree-granting institutions and national thesis networks.**
[NDLTD's FAQ](https://ndltd.org/thesis-resources/faqs/) describes a union catalog
made available to service providers and directs users to its current Find ETDs
resources; its navigation currently points Global ETD Search to OATD. Treat this
as a directory/coverage route, not evidence of a turnkey NDLTD keyword API.
Cross-reference university origins through OpenDOAR.

| Research track | Where to look and how to expand |
| --- | --- |
| International | Follow NDLTD's member/resource links to national thesis services and their contributing universities. Sample different languages and degree systems; a national portal is an index unless it hosts the authoritative deposit. |
| USA | Inspect official university library ETD policies and institutional repositories. Check whether the institution supplies open deposits or only points to a commercial dissertation service. University departments are not extra origins when their theses share one maintained catalog. |
| India | Begin with Shodhganga through [INFLIBNET's official initiatives](https://www.inflibnet.ac.in/activities/), then follow university links. Use the official university directory's state/category browsing to fill geographic gaps. [IndCat's documented features](https://indcat.inflibnet.ac.in/index.php/main/features) include thesis discovery and Shodhganga links, but a bibliographic record is not itself a readable thesis. |

Search recipes:

```text
site:{university-domain} ("electronic theses" OR dissertation OR thesis) repository
"{university name}" (OAI-PMH OR "metadata harvesting")
"{state or university}" (शोधप्रबंध OR ஆய்வேடு) repository
```

The first ten candidates should include four Indian university origins from
different states, two US universities and four institutions in other regions.
Select two deep reviews with different repository platforms/languages. Build the
next batches from uncovered degree institutions, not repeated national-portal
collections. Five discovery regions with 20 qualified institution catalogs each
is a research allocation toward 100, subject to actual conversion and overlap.

**Retrieval strategy.** Verify attributed aggregator coverage with known thesis
titles first. Otherwise inspect the repository's advertised OAI-PMH/export or
documented API. OAI-PMH requires an import and local title/topic search; it is not
a live keyword endpoint. Discover actual supported routes and versions instead
of guessing DSpace paths. Start with a bounded, disclosed metadata subset using
the existing catalog approach; no new hosted database is prerequisite.

**Category-specific proof.** Check complete dissertation versus abstract/synopsis,
degree, university, award year, native handle and content language. Sample a
multi-file/chapter thesis, embargoed deposit, scanned document and duplicate
national/institutional copy. Search Hindi/Tamil titles in native script where
claimed; compare transliteration separately. Successful retrieval of a title page
or one chapter does not establish access to the whole thesis. Document OCR/full-text
limitations, withdrawn records and how embargo changes will be refreshed.

## C07 — Preprints and working papers

**Use two different discovery paths: disciplinary servers and institutional series.**
[ASAPbio's server directory](https://asapbio.org/preprint-servers/) describes
server scope and practices. [RePEc's archive directory](https://ideas.repec.org/archives.html)
identifies institutional archive providers, but explicitly says its listing is
not current. Follow its archive templates and each institution's current site;
do not derive today's coverage totals from that list.

| Research track | Where to look and how to expand |
| --- | --- |
| International | Use ASAPbio for disciplinary server leads, SciELO's preprint link for regional coverage, and RePEc archive/provider links for economics and social-science working-paper collections. Sample more than one discipline. |
| USA | Follow university/research-center working-paper series and government research-unit publications from their official sites. Record whether a series is independently maintained or part of the institution's existing repository origin. |
| India | Follow Indian institutions in RePEc and the INFLIBNET university directory; inspect economics, management, engineering and agricultural research repositories. Include native-language series where actually present; an English institutional website does not prove English-only holdings. |

Search recipes:

```text
site:{institution-domain} ("working papers" OR "discussion papers" OR preprints)
"{series name}" (ReDIF OR metadata OR repository OR API)
"{discipline}" "{country}" "preprint server"
```

For the first ten origins, investigate four Indian institution collections, three
international disciplinary servers and three institutional series from other
regions, including the USA. Deep-review one server and one working-paper archive.
To approach 100, replenish both paths in batches of 25 and deduplicate operators.
There may not be 100 suitable independent preprint servers; institutional
working-paper catalogs supply a distinct, valid part of this category. One
university's many series still count as one catalog origin under the main rules.

**Retrieval strategy.** Prefer existing attributed aggregator search where its
coverage passes. The [bioRxiv/medRxiv API documentation](https://api.biorxiv.org/)
supports date-window/DOI metadata retrieval and version information; it is not a
generic keyword search interface. A permitted bounded metadata import can make
that feed searchable locally. [RePEc's metadata policy](https://ideas.repec.org/getdata.html)
prefers publisher archives/ReDIF over website scraping and requires prior contact
for commercial use. Review applicability before use; no outreach is sent as part
of this plan. Direct arXiv automation remains deferred under the current plan.

**Category-specific proof.** Search five known preprints/working papers, including
an older version, updated version, published successor, withdrawn item and a
paper without DOI where those cases exist. Preserve native handle, series/number,
version date and exact reading destination. Publication relations are links,
not a reason to merge distinct versions. Test topic results for industry terms
and label preprints clearly; being publicly readable is not peer-review evidence.

## Handoff and research limits

Each ten-candidate batch produces the origin register, two completed qualification
records, a category benchmark, unsupported-query notes and the next directory
expansion. Report aggregate overlap across C03/C06/C07 before estimating work.
Scale only after measuring pass rates and useful new coverage.

This review inspected official directory/protocol documentation, not production
API behavior, source-login access or complete catalogs. The old OpenAlex docs URL
failed after redirect; the linked Help Center route worked. RePEc's root page
returned a gateway error while its archive/policy pages worked. These are tooling
observations, not evidence of source-wide downtime. Current prices, permission,
freshness and per-origin free access still require qualification before enablement.

# Source catalog and connection options

Research date: 2026-10-31. Update 2026-11-01: [additional probes and Book Dash delivery](ADDITIONAL_SOURCES.md). Reconstructed for MyBookshelf-web; see [provenance](README.md#repository-transfer-and-evidence-provenance) and [historical API observations](evidence.json). Provider rules and quotas need rechecking before enabling a connector.

**Roles:** host supplies the reading destination; index describes items hosted elsewhere; resolver finds a location from an identifier. Some providers perform several roles.

**Effort:** low = documented search and straightforward mapping; medium = imports, XML, edition/access reconciliation or account setup; high = feed agreement or unresolved public integration. These are relative integration estimates, not delivery promises.

**Priority:** P0 = initial implementation; P1 = subsequent coverage; P2 = investigate or arrange access. No public API verified means this research did not establish one, not that none exists.

## 1. General ebooks and public-domain literature

| Source / role | How the app can search it | Reading destination and access distinction | Credentials, constraints, effort / priority |

No generic HTML scraper is needed for the first release. Search-engine scraping, subscription bypasses and unauthorized shadow libraries are excluded. Build a **metadata discovery service with outbound reading links**. Use a hybrid of locally indexed metadata catalogs and a small number of live search adapters. The app should not download or serve the books or papers themselves.

This is feasible with free sources. The difficult parts are deciding whether a specific edition is actually readable, keeping source permissions and quotas current, and combining overlapping records without losing versions or translations. Free content does not imply an unlimited free search API.

## Recommendation

Start with **Free books** and **Research papers**. Add **Textbooks & learning** through the Open Textbook Library catalog, then a curated **Children's books** collection. Treat language, subject, reading level, format, and access conditions as separate filters rather than mutually exclusive categories.

| Open Textbook Library | Official CSV/JSON metadata; local search | Documented CC0 catalog for educational material |
| DOAJ | Live article search | OA journal articles with publisher full-text links |
| Europe PMC | Live search and record details | Biomedical literature with explicit full-text/OA fields |
| arXiv | Atom API behind a shared request queue | Direct preprint coverage with clearly labeled versions |
| OpenAlex | Live search after key/budget verification | Broad multidisciplinary discovery and OA locations; usage is metered |
| DOAB / OAPEN | Metadata imports and OAI-PMH updates | Scholarly books and chapters; next import candidates |

Reuse Google Books and Open Library selectively to enrich book records and resolve existing saved books to candidate free editions. Their general catalogs contain previews, borrowing offers, and metadata-only records; they should not define the free-reading collection by themselves.

## What the original checks established

Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.

These were small one-time checks, not integration, rights, uptime, completeness, or user-country tests. Important counterexamples:

- An Open Library work returned `ebook_access: public` alongside many Internet Archive identifiers. That does not identify which edition is freely readable.
- A HAL hit had a record URL and DOI but no `fileMain_s`: a repository hit is not necessarily full text.
- Zenodo returned a dataset; item-type filtering is essential.
- DOAJ supplied an older HTTP publisher URL; metadata alone does not prove the destination still works.
- Semantic Scholar returned **429**, and Gutendex timed out. Those checks do not establish general service availability.
- Some documentation URLs moved; corrected DOAB/OAPEN URLs appear in the catalog. Some sites returned only a JavaScript shell. NCERT/ERIC/OER Commons could not be fully inspected.

Two current details make older integration advice unreliable: Standard Ebooks' full OPDS feeds require membership/access arrangements, and Unpaywall's documentation said its title-search endpoint retired on **2026-09-18**. Use Unpaywall for DOI resolution and another index for search. Recheck these policies before implementation.

## Credentials and implementation inputs

No additional credentials are needed to review this plan. The original Google Books free-ebook query succeeded using the configured key. For implementation:

1. Verify **`OPENALEX_API_KEY`** in the backend. The replacement environment reports the variable configured; no authenticated OpenAlex request was made during this repository transfer. At the research date the free account included $1/day of API usage, roughly 1,000 ordinary search requests before caching. Disable paid overages unless deliberately budgeted.
2. Choose a real **application contact email** for request identification and, if enabled, Unpaywall's required `email` parameter. No email was invented, registered, or sent during this work.
3. Optional later: Semantic Scholar, BHL and Europeana keys; CORE upgrade/eligibility confirmation. Standard Ebooks feed access and children's/OER catalog feeds need provider-specific arrangements.

Assumptions: global discovery with explicit language/country context; lawful public hosts; verified free source login is allowed (owner clarification 2026-11-01), labelled separately from anonymous reading; no full-text hosting, subscription purchases, or library-card integration. Existing India library coverage makes NCERT, DIKSHA, StoryWeaver and Shodhganga useful follow-ups, but their discovery integrations are not assumed ready.

source status, partial/unavailable/empty/limit/loading states, the children's
pilot and a desktop layout. Records on the boards are samples.

Owner decisions on the proposal:

1. Keep the four app tabs. Free to read and Papers are scopes inside Search.
2. Free books and papers can be saved to the shelf. Storage for items without
   ISBNs still needs an engineering design before implementation.
3. Results with unclear access are hidden by default and clearly marked when shown.
4. No "include previews and loans" option in the first release.
5. When the broad paper index is at its daily limit, say so plainly
   ("at today's limit") without naming the provider.
6. Children's pilot: English, Hindi and Tamil, using each publisher's own levels.
7. A free book links back to the reader's library by title search, without
   treating the two as the same edition.
8. Rights text stays generic for now: source statement plus "check your
   country's rules", rather than a per-country claim.
9. Use the existing public contact for request identification. Use is
   non-commercial. Traffic expectations and quotas will be set later.

The owner clarified that free source login is acceptable and asked Codex to
research additional sources. Three real StoryWeaver records in English, Hindi
and Tamil are now reviewed and searchable with an explicit free-account label;
no source account was created. Book Dash adds 30 real English-language editions
with public anonymous reading links. These are source-native metadata records,
not fictional board samples. The existing OpenAlex key was accepted by its API;
Redis setup is postponed, so live paper enablement remains deferred.
See [children’s review](CHILDREN_REVIEW.md), [additional sources](ADDITIONAL_SOURCES.md)
and [validation](VALIDATION.md). All source flags still default off pending the
intended hosted release checks; local metadata searches need no hosted store.
